title.zh: 卷二百零六 列傳第一百三十一 外戚
title.en: Volume 206 Biographies 131: Families of Imperial Consorts
title.raw: 卷二百零六 列傳第一百三十一 外戚 Volume 206 Biographies 131: Families of Imperial Consorts

sentences.zh: 凡外戚成敗，視主德何如。

translations.literal: In general whether maternal kin succeed or fail depends on what the sovereign's virtue is like.
translations.idiomatic: Whether imperial in-laws rise or fall has always depended on the moral caliber of the ruler.

sentences.zh: 主賢則共其榮，主否則先受其禍。

translations.literal: If the lord is worthy then they share his glory; if the lord is unworthy then they first receive the disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Under a capable sovereign they share in his glory; under a bad one they are the first to suffer ruin.

sentences.zh: 故太宗檢貴幸，裁賞賜，貞觀時，內裏無敗家。

translations.literal: Therefore Taizong restrained the honored and favored, trimmed rewards and gifts, and in the Zhenguan era the inner palace had no families that ruined the state.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong therefore kept favored kin in check and limited their largesse, so that throughout the Zhenguan reign no consort clan brought the house down.

sentences.zh: 高、中二宗，柄移艷私，產亂朝廷，武、韋諸族，耄嬰頸血，一日同汙鐵刃。

translations.literal: Under the two emperors Gaozong and Zhongzong power shifted to beautiful private favorites, producing chaos in the court; the Wu and Wei clans, old and infant alike with blood at the neck, in one day together stained the iron blade.
translations.idiomatic: Under Gaozong and Zhongzong, power passed to illicit favorites of the inner quarters and threw the court into turmoil; the Wu and Wei kin, from elders to infants, had their throats cut and on a single day shared the same bloody steel.

sentences.zh: 玄宗初年，法行近親，裏表修敕。

translations.literal: In the early years of Xuanzong the law was applied to close kin and relatives inside and outside the clan were disciplined.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xuanzong's reign the law was enforced even upon close relatives, and consort kin were kept in proper order.

sentences.zh: 天寶奪明，委政妃宗，階召反虜，遂喪天下。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era enlightenment was lost, government was entrusted to the consort's clan, step by step rebels were summoned, and thus the realm was lost.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianbao dimmed the emperor's clarity, power was handed to the consort clan, traitors were called in stage by stage, and the empire was lost.

sentences.zh: 楊氏之誅，噍類不遺，蓋數十年之寵，不賞一日之慘，甲第厚貲，無救同坎之悲，寧不哀哉！

translations.literal: At the execution of the Yang clan not a mouth was left, for decades of favor were not rewarded with a day of mercy; mansions and great wealth could not save the grief of sharing one pit—is it not pitiful!
translations.idiomatic: When the Yang clan were put to the sword, none were spared; decades of imperial favor bought them not a day's leniency, and though they had lived in great estates heaped with treasure, nothing could keep them from a common grave—how lamentable!

sentences.zh: 代、德而降，閹尹參嬖，後宮雖多，無赫赫顯門，亦無刀鋸大戮。

translations.literal: From the Daizong and Dezong reigns downward eunuchs and stewards shared in favor; though the rear palace had many women, there were no illustriously famous clans, nor great executions by blade and saw.
translations.idiomatic: From Daizong and Dezong onward, eunuchs and palace stewards shared imperial favor; though the inner quarters had many consorts, there were no towering consort houses—and no wholesale slaughter by the executioners either.

sentences.zh: 故用福甚者得禍酷，取名少者蒙責輕，理所固然。

translations.literal: Therefore those who used great blessing received extreme calamity; those who sought little fame bore light blame—it is reason's constant way.
translations.idiomatic: Those who grasped the greatest favor suffered the fiercest ruin; those who claimed little glory escaped with lighter blame—as reason demands.

sentences.zh: 若乃長孫無忌之功，武平一之識，吳漵之忠，弗緣內寵者，自見別傳。

translations.literal: As for Zhangsun Wuji's merit, Wu Pingyi's discernment, and Wu Qian's loyalty—not owing to inner favor—each is seen in a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Zhangsun Wuji for achievement, Wu Pingyi for judgment, and Wu Qian for loyalty, who rose without inner-palace patronage, are treated in other biographies.

sentences.zh: 獨孤懷恩

translations.literal: Dugu Huai'en
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Huai'en

sentences.zh: 獨孤懷恩，元貞皇后弟之子也。

translations.literal: Dugu Huai'en was a son of the younger brother of Empress Yuanzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Huai'en was the son of Empress Yuanzhen's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 父整，仕隋為涿郡太守。

translations.literal: His father Zheng served the Sui as Administrator of Zhuo Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zheng had served the Sui as prefect of Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 懷恩之幼，隋文帝獻皇后以侄養宮中。

translations.literal: When Huai'en was young, Emperor Wen of Sui's Empress Xian raised him as a nephew in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In his childhood Empress Xian of Emperor Wen of Sui took him into the palace and raised him as her nephew.

sentences.zh: 逮長，稍學記書，而居財不訾，喜交豪猾博徒。

translations.literal: When he grew up he learned a little record-keeping and writing, but he did not assess his property and liked to associate with bold scoundrels and gamblers.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew he picked up some clerical learning, yet he kept no proper accounts of his wealth and consorted with swaggering gamblers.

sentences.zh: 為鄠令，以疾免。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Hu County and was dismissed on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He became magistrate of Hu but was removed because of illness.

sentences.zh: 高祖平京師，拜長安令，頗嚴明，如職而辨。

translations.literal: When Gaozu pacified the capital region he appointed him magistrate of Chang'an; he was quite strict and clear, performing his duties with discernment.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu took the capital he made him magistrate of Chang'an, where he governed with notable strictness and sound judgment.

sentences.zh: 帝受禪，擢工部尚書。

translations.literal: When the emperor received the abdication he was promoted to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the throne he was raised to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 初，虞州刺史韋義節擊堯君素於蒲州，不克，帝遣懷恩代將。

translations.literal: At first Yu Prefecture inspector Wei Yijie attacked Yao Junsu at Pu Prefecture without success, and the emperor sent Huai'en to replace him as commander.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yu prefect Wei Yijie had attacked Yao Junsu at Pu without success, and the emperor sent Huai'en to take command in his place.

sentences.zh: 性貪，寡算略，數戰無功，士喪沮，詔書切責，而懷恩稍怨望。

translations.literal: By nature he was greedy and lacked strategy; he fought many times without achievement, the soldiers lost heart, an edict sharply rebuked him, and Huai'en gradually grew resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Greedy and short on strategy, he fought repeatedly without success until his troops lost heart; the emperor's stern rebuke left him increasingly bitter.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗與戲曰：「弟姑子悉有天下，次當爾邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor once jested with him, saying: "Your younger cousins by the aunt have all possessed the realm—should you be next?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once teased him, saying, "Your cousins on your aunt's side have all held the realm—is it your turn next?

sentences.zh: 懷恩內喜，以為天命。

translations.literal: Huai'en rejoiced inwardly and took it as Heaven's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en was secretly delighted and took this as a sign of destiny.

sentences.zh: 既而居忽忽，咤曰：「我家渠獨女子富貴也？」

translations.literal: Thereafter he lived in restless gloom and exclaimed: "Must our house alone have its wealth and honor through women?
translations.idiomatic: Soon he grew restless and cried out, "Must our clan alone win wealth and rank through its women?

sentences.zh: 因謀亂。

translations.literal: He therefore plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: And so he plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 是時，虞鄉南山多宿盜，而劉武周使宋金剛略澮州，帝發關中軍屬秦王，屯柏壁。

translations.literal: At that time on the southern hills of Yuxiang there were many long-established bandits, while Liu Wuzhou sent Song Jingang to overrun Fen Prefecture; the emperor dispatched Guanzhong troops under the Prince of Qin and encamped at Baiyu.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the southern hills of Yuxiang were thick with veteran bandits, while Liu Wuzhou sent Song Jingang to overrun Fen; the emperor sent Guanzhong forces under the Prince of Qin to encamp at Baiyu.

sentences.zh: 由是懷恩與麾下元君寶、解令榮靜謀引王行本軍與武周連和，割河東以啖之，引群賊取永豐倉，絕秦王餉道，長驅三輔。

translations.literal: Thereupon Huai'en with his subordinates Yuan Junbao and Xie Lingrong secretly plotted to bring Wang Xingben's army into alliance with Wuzhou, cede Hedong to feed them, lead the bandit hosts to seize Yongfeng Granary, cut the Prince of Qin's supply route, and drive straight into the Three Metropolises.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en then conspired quietly with his officers Yuan Junbao and Xie Lingrong to join Wang Xingben's forces to Liu Wuzhou, yield Hedong as bait, rally the bandits to seize Yongfeng Granary, sever the Prince of Qin's supply line, and march straight on the capital region.

sentences.zh: 會君素死，而行本得其兵，部畫已定，而夏人呂崇茂殺縣令應武周。

translations.literal: It happened that Junsu died and Xingben took over his troops; the deployment was already set, but a man of Xia, Lü Chongmao, killed the county magistrate and submitted to Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Junsu died just then and Xingben took over his army; the plan was already laid when Lü Chongmao of Xia killed his magistrate and went over to Liu Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝敕懷恩與永安王孝基、陜州總管於筠、內史侍郎唐儉擊夏，為金剛所掩，諸將皆沒於賊。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Huai'en with Prince of Yong'an Xiaoji, Shaan overall commander Yu Yun, and Secretariat Vice Director Tang Jian to strike Xia; they were ambushed by Jingang and all the generals were lost to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Huai'en, Prince of Yong'an Xiaoji, Shaan commander Yu Yun, and Vice Director Tang Jian against Xia, but Jingang ambushed them and every commander fell into rebel hands.

sentences.zh: 君寶與開府劉讓私侮懷恩曰：「不早舉大事，以及斯辱也。」

translations.literal: Junbao and Defender-in-Chief Liu Rang privately insulted Huai'en, saying: "Because you did not rise early in a great affair, we have come to this disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: Junbao and Defender Liu Rang privately taunted Huai'en: "Had you moved earlier on the great design, we would not have suffered this humiliation.

sentences.zh: 故謀浸露。

translations.literal: Thus the plot gradually leaked out.
translations.idiomatic: And so the conspiracy slowly came to light.

sentences.zh: 及秦王敗武周於美良川，懷恩逃歸，帝命率師攻蒲州。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Qin defeated Wuzhou at Meiliang River, Huai'en fled back and the emperor ordered him to lead troops against Pu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After the Prince of Qin routed Liu Wuzhou at Meiliang River, Huai'en escaped home and was ordered to lead an assault on Pu.

sentences.zh: 君寶聞曰：「王者不死，果其然！」

translations.literal: Junbao heard and said: "A true king does not die—it is indeed so!
translations.idiomatic: Junbao heard this and said, "A true king cannot be killed—so it proves!

sentences.zh: 唐儉知狀。

translations.literal: Tang Jian learned the situation.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Jian learned what was afoot.

sentences.zh: 會武周還劉讓求罷兵，因白髮懷恩等奸。

translations.literal: It happened that Wuzhou returned and Liu Rang asked to cease fighting, and thereby reported Huai'en's treachery and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Wuzhou withdrew, Liu Rang sued for peace and disclosed Huai'en's treason.

sentences.zh: 於時行本舉蒲州降，懷恩勒兵入城，帝方濟河而讓至，具得反狀。

translations.literal: At that time Xingben raised Pu Prefecture in surrender; Huai'en drove his troops into the city; the emperor was just crossing the river when Rang arrived and fully obtained the evidence of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Xingben had just surrendered Pu when Huai'en marched in; the emperor was crossing the river as Rang arrived with full proof of the plot.

sentences.zh: 帝召之，懷恩不知也，單舟以來，即縛之，窮索黨與，縊死於獄，以首徇華陰市，籍入其家。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned him; Huai'en did not know and came in a single boat; he was immediately bound, his accomplices thoroughly sought out, strangled to death in prison, his head displayed in Huayin market, and his household registered and confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned him; unaware, Huai'en came alone in a small boat and was seized at once; his accomplices were hunted down, he was strangled in prison, his head was exposed in Huayin market, and his property was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 武士彟

translations.literal: Wu Shiyao
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shiyao

sentences.zh: 武士彟字信，世殖貲，喜交結。

translations.literal: Wu Shiyao, style Xin, for generations amassed wealth and delighted in forming connections.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shiyao, styled Xin, came from a family that had long grown rich by trade and was fond of cultivating ties.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘗領屯汾、晉，休其家，因被顧接。

translations.literal: Gaozu once led encampments in Fen and Jin, lodged at his house, and thereby received his attentive reception.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu once commanded troops in Fen and Jin he stayed at Wu's home and came to know him well.

sentences.zh: 後留守太原，引為行軍司鎧參軍。

translations.literal: Later, when he remained to guard Taiyuan, he brought him in as campaign staff armor aide.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as regent at Taiyuan, he took him on as an aide in the armor bureau of the campaign staff.

sentences.zh: 募兵既集，以劉弘基、長孫順德統之。

translations.literal: When the recruited soldiers were assembled, Liu Hongji and Zhangsun Shunde were put in command of them.
translations.idiomatic: Once the levies were gathered, Liu Hongji and Zhangsun Shunde were placed over them.

sentences.zh: 王威、高君雅私謂士訄曰：「弘基等皆背征三衛，罪當死，奈何授之兵？

translations.literal: Wang Wei and Gao Junya privately said to Wu Shiyao: "Hongji and the rest all deserted the Three Guards levy—crime deserving death—how can you hand them troops?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wei and Gao Junya privately told Wu Shiyao, "Hongji and the others deserted the Three Guards levy, a capital offense—why give them command of troops?

sentences.zh: 吾且劾系之。」

translations.literal: We shall impeach and bind them.
translations.idiomatic: We mean to impeach and arrest them.

sentences.zh: 士卬皞曰：「此皆唐公客，若爾，必大有嫌。」

translations.literal: Wu Shiyao said: "These are all Duke of Tang's guests; if you do so, there will surely be great suspicion."
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shiyao replied, "They are all the Duke of Tang's men; act thus and you will surely earn his deep mistrust."

sentences.zh: 故威等疑不發。

translations.literal: Therefore Wei and the others hesitated and did not act.
translations.idiomatic: Wei and his party therefore hesitated and did not move.

sentences.zh: 會司兵參軍田德平欲勸威劾募人狀，士訄脅謂曰：「討捕兵悉隸唐公，威、君雅無與，徒寄坐耳，何能為？」

translations.literal: It happened that Staff Officer Tian Deping wished to urge Wei to impeach the status of the recruits; Wu Shiyao coerced him, saying: "All the punitive-recruit troops belong to the Duke of Tang; Wei and Junya have no part—they merely sit by delegation—what can they do?
translations.idiomatic: When Staff Officer Tian Deping tried to urge Wei to impeach the recruits, Wu Shiyao intimidated him, saying, "Every soldier raised for the campaign answers to the Duke of Tang; Wei and Junya have no real authority—they only hold their posts in name—what can they do?

sentences.zh: 德平亦止。

translations.literal: Deping also stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Deping too held back.

sentences.zh: 兵起，士卬皞不與謀也。

translations.literal: When the army rose, Wu Shiyao did not take part in the planning.
translations.idiomatic: When arms were raised, Wu Shiyao had not joined the conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 以大將軍府鎧曹參軍從平京師，為光祿大夫、義原郡公。

translations.literal: As Grand General's Staff armor bureau aide he followed in pacifying the capital region and was made Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and Duke of Yiyuan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the campaign to pacify the capital as an aide in the Grand General's armor bureau and was made Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and Duke of Yiyuan.

sentences.zh: 自言嘗夢帝騎而上天，帝笑曰：「爾故王威黨也，以能罷系劉弘基等，其意可錄，且嘗禮我，故酬汝以官。

translations.literal: He said himself that he once dreamed the emperor riding and ascending to Heaven; the emperor laughed and said: "You were formerly of Wang Wei's party; because you could stop the binding of Liu Hongji and the rest, your intent is worth recording, and you once honored me, therefore I reward you with office.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed he had dreamed the emperor riding up to Heaven; the emperor laughed and said, "You were once Wang Wei's man; because you kept Liu Hongji and the others from being arrested your intent is worth noting, and because you once treated me with respect I repay you with rank.

sentences.zh: 今胡迂妄媚我邪？」

translations.literal: Why now do you absurdly flatter me?
translations.idiomatic: Why do you now fawn on me with such absurd tales?

sentences.zh: 累遷工部尚書，進封應國公，歷利、荊二州都督。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Minister of Works, advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Ying state, and served as overall commander of Li and Jing prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through repeated promotions to Minister of Works, was advanced to Duke of Ying, and served as military governor of Li and Jing.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈禮部尚書，謚曰定。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was given Minister of Rites and the posthumous title Ding.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Minister of Rites with the posthumous name Ding.

sentences.zh: 高宗永徽中，以士↓仲女為皇后，故崇贈并州都督、司徒、周國公。

translations.literal: In the Yonghui era of Gaozong, because Wu Shiyao's daughter became empress, he was honored posthumously with Overall Commander of Bing Prefecture, Minister of Education, and Duke of Zhou state.
translations.idiomatic: In Gaozong's Yonghui reign, when Wu Shiyao's daughter became empress, he was posthumously raised to overall commander of Bing, Minister of Education, and Duke of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 咸亨中，加贈太尉兼太子太師、太原郡王，配享高祖廟廷，列功臣上。

translations.literal: In the Xianheng era he was further given Grand Commandant with concurrent Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Prince of Taiyuan commandery, with sacrifice in Gaozu's temple court, ranked above the merit subjects.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xianheng era he was further made Grand Commandant and Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, Prince of Taiyuan, granted sacrifice in Gaozu's temple, and ranked above the merit subjects.

sentences.zh: 后監朝，尊為忠孝太皇，建崇先府，置官屬，追王五世。

translations.literal: When the empress supervised the court she honored him as Loyal and Filial Grand Emperor, established the Chongxian Office, appointed officials, and ennobled five generations retroactively.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress held court she honored him as Loyal and Filial Grand Emperor, founded the Chongxian Office with its own staff, and ennobled five generations of ancestors.

sentences.zh: 后革命，更於東都立武氏七廟，追冊為帝，諸妣皆隨帝號曰皇后。

translations.literal: When the empress changed the dynasty she further established the Wu clan's seven temples in the eastern capital, posthumously enfeoffed him as emperor, and all the mothers followed the emperor's title as empress.
translations.idiomatic: When she changed the dynasty she built seven Wu ancestral temples in the eastern capital, posthumously enthroned him as emperor, and gave all his wives the title of empress to match.

sentences.zh: 先天中，有詔削士卬皞偽號，仍為太原王，廟遂廢。

translations.literal: In the Xiantian era an edict stripped Wu Shiyao's spurious titles, restored him as Prince of Taiyuan, and the temple was then abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiantian era an edict stripped Wu Shiyao's usurped titles, restored him only as Prince of Taiyuan, and the temple was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 始，士訄娶相裏氏，生子元慶、元爽。

translations.literal: At first Wu Shiyao married the Xiangli clan and bore sons Yuangqing and Yuanshuang.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shiyao had first married a woman of the Xiangli clan and had sons Yuangqing and Yuanshuang.

sentences.zh: 又娶楊氏，生三女。

translations.literal: He also married the Yang clan and bore three daughters.
translations.idiomatic: He then married Lady Yang, who bore three daughters.

sentences.zh: 元女妻賀蘭氏，早寡。

translations.literal: The eldest daughter married the Helan clan and was widowed early.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest daughter married into the Helan clan and was widowed young.

sentences.zh: 季女妻郭氏，不顯。

translations.literal: The youngest daughter married the Guo clan and did not become prominent.
translations.idiomatic: The youngest daughter married into the Guo clan and left no mark on history.

sentences.zh: 士卬皞卒後，諸子事楊不盡禮，銜之。

translations.literal: After Wu Shiyao died his sons did not treat Yang with full courtesy, and she harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu Shiyao's death his sons failed to show Lady Yang full respect, and she bore a grudge.

sentences.zh: 后立，封楊代國夫人，進為榮國，后姊韓國夫人。

translations.literal: When the empress was established, Yang was enfeoffed Lady of Dai state, advanced to Rong state, and the empress's elder sister as Lady of Han state.
translations.idiomatic: Once the empress was enthroned, Lady Yang was made Lady of Dai and then of Rong, and the empress's elder sister was made Lady of Han.

sentences.zh: 於時元慶已官宗正少卿，元爽少府少監，兄子惟良衛尉少卿。

translations.literal: At that time Yuangqing already held office as Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court, Yuanshuang as Vice Director of the Palace Storehouses, and the elder brother's son Weiliang as Vice Director of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: By then Yuangqing was Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court, Yuanshuang Vice Director of the Palace Storehouses, and their cousin Weiliang Vice Director of the Guards.

sentences.zh: 楊諷后上疏出元慶等於外，以示退讓。

translations.literal: Yang admonished the empress to memorialize sending Yuangqing and the rest outside, to show yielding.
translations.idiomatic: Yang urged the empress to petition that Yuangqing and the others be sent away from court as a show of modest restraint.

sentences.zh: 由是元慶斥龍州，元爽濠州，惟良始州。

translations.literal: Thereby Yuangqing was banished to Long Prefecture, Yuanshuang to Hao Prefecture, and Weiliang to Shi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yuangqing was sent to Long, Yuanshuang to Hao, and Weiliang to Shi.

sentences.zh: 元慶死，元爽流振州。

translations.literal: Yuangqing died; Yuanshuang was exiled to Zhen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yuangqing died, and Yuanshuang was banished to Zhen.

sentences.zh: 乾封時，惟良及弟淄州刺史懷運與嶽牧集泰山下，於是韓國有女在宮中，帝尤愛幸。

translations.literal: In the Qianfeng era Weiliang and his younger brother Huaiyun, prefect of Zi, with the mountain prefects gathered below Mount Tai; at that time the Lady of Han state had a daughter in the palace whom the emperor especially favored.
translations.idiomatic: During Qianfeng, Weiliang and his brother Huaiyun, prefect of Zi, joined the frontier lords at Mount Tai; the Lady of Han then had a daughter in the palace whom the emperor especially favored.

sentences.zh: 后欲並殺之，即導帝幸其母所，惟良等上食，后寘堇焉，賀蘭食之，暴死。

translations.literal: The empress wished to kill them all together; she guided the emperor to visit their mother's place; Weiliang and the rest presented food; the empress placed aconite in it; Helan ate and died suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: The empress meant to destroy them all at once; she led the emperor to their mother's home, and when Weiliang and the others served the meal she poisoned it with aconite; the Helan woman ate and died on the spot.

sentences.zh: 后歸罪惟良等，誅之，諷有司改姓「蝮氏」，絕屬籍。

translations.literal: The empress placed the blame on Weiliang and the rest, executed them, and hinted to the authorities to change their surname to "Viper Clan" and cut them from the clan registers.
translations.idiomatic: She blamed Weiliang and his kin, had them executed, and prompted the authorities to change their surname to "Viper" and strike them from the registers.

sentences.zh: 元爽緣坐死，家屬投嶺外。

translations.literal: Yuanshuang died by implication in the case; his household was cast beyond the ranges.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshuang was executed by association, and his family was sent beyond the southern ranges.

sentences.zh: 后取賀蘭敏之為士訄後，賜氏武，襲封，擢累左侍極、蘭臺太史令，與名儒李嗣真等參與刊撰。

translations.literal: The empress took Helan Minzhi as Wu Shiyao's heir, granted the surname Wu, had him inherit the enfeoffment, and repeatedly promoted him to Left Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Astrological Bureau of the Orchid Terrace, joining famous scholars such as Li Sizhen in compilation work.
translations.idiomatic: The empress adopted Helan Minzhi as Wu Shiyao's heir, gave him the surname Wu and the family title, and raised him through Left Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Astrological Bureau, where he worked with scholars such as Li Sizhen on editorial projects.

sentences.zh: 敏之韶秀自喜，烝於榮國，挾所愛，佻橫多過失；

translations.literal: Minzhi was youthful and handsome and pleased with himself; he committed incest with the Lady of Rong state, relied on those he favored, and was frivolous and overbearing with many faults;
translations.idiomatic: Minzhi was young, handsome, and vain; he had an affair with Lady Rong, abused his favorites, and with frivolous arrogance committed one offense after another;

sentences.zh: 榮國卒，后出珍幣建佛廬僥福，敏之乾匿自用；

translations.literal: when the Lady of Rong died the empress issued precious goods to build a Buddhist hall to seek blessing, and Minzhi embezzled them for his own use;
translations.idiomatic: when Lady Rong died the empress sent precious funds to build a Buddhist hall for merit, and Minzhi diverted them to himself;

sentences.zh: 司衛少卿楊思儉女選為太子妃，告婚期矣，敏之聞其美，強私焉；

translations.literal: the daughter of Vice Director of the Guards Yang Sijian was chosen as the crown prince's consort and the wedding date was announced; Minzhi heard of her beauty and forcibly violated her;
translations.idiomatic: the daughter of Vice Director Yang Sijian had been chosen as crown princess and the wedding day set, but Minzhi, hearing of her beauty, forced himself upon her;

sentences.zh: 楊喪未畢，褫衰粗，奏音樂；

translations.literal: before Yang's mourning was finished he cast off coarse mourning, and performed music;
translations.idiomatic: before Lady Yang's mourning was over he cast off his mourning garb and had music played;

sentences.zh: 太平公主往來外家，宮人從者，敏之悉逼亂之。

translations.literal: when Princess Taiping came and went at her mother's family, the palace women who followed her—Minzhi forced and debauched them all.
translations.idiomatic: when Princess Taiping visited her mother's kin, he violated every palace woman in her train.

sentences.zh: 后叠數怒，至此暴其惡，流雷州，表復故姓，道中自經死。

translations.literal: The empress had been angry many times; at this point she exposed his wickedness, exiled him to Lei Prefecture, memorialized restoring his former surname, and on the road he hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: The empress had long been furious; now she exposed his crimes, exiled him to Lei, petitioned to restore his original surname, and on the way he hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 乃還元爽之子承嗣奉士皞後，宗屬悉原。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yuanshuang's son Chengsi was returned to serve as Wu Shiyao's heir, and the whole clan was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshuang's son Chengsi was then brought back as Wu Shiyao's heir, and the whole clan was restored.

sentences.zh: 士訄兄士梭、士逸。

translations.literal: Wu Shiyao's elder brothers Shileng and Shiyi.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shiyao's elder brothers Shileng and Shiyi.

sentences.zh: 士棱，字彥威，少柔願，力於田。

translations.literal: Shileng, style Yanwei, in youth was gentle and compliant and exerted himself in farming.
translations.idiomatic: Shileng, styled Yanwei, was gentle and dutiful in youth and devoted himself to the fields.

sentences.zh: 官司農少卿，宣城縣公，常主苑囿農稼事。

translations.literal: In office he was Vice Director of the Ministry of Agriculture, Duke of Xuancheng county, and regularly oversaw parklands and agricultural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Vice Director of Agriculture, Duke of Xuancheng, and routinely managed the palace farms and parklands.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈潭州都督，陪葬獻陵。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously given Overall Commander of Tan Prefecture and burial attendant at Xian Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made overall commander of Tan, with burial at Xian's mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 士逸，字逖，有戰功，為齊王府戶曹參軍，六安縣公。

translations.literal: Shiyi, style Ti, had military achievement, served as Household Bureau aide in the Prince of Qi's establishment, and was Duke of Lu'an county.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyi, styled Ti, won distinction in battle, served as household aide in the Prince of Qi's establishment, and was Duke of Lu'an.

sentences.zh: 從王守太原，為劉武周所執，嘗遣間人陳破賊計。

translations.literal: He followed the prince in guarding Taiyuan, was seized by Liu Wuzhou, and once sent an agent to present a plan for defeating the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the prince in holding Taiyuan, was captured by Liu Wuzhou, and once sent a secret messenger with a plan to break the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊平，擢授益州行臺左丞，數言當世得失，高祖嘉納之。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified he was promoted and appointed Left Assistant of the Yizhou field secretariat, repeatedly spoke on the gains and losses of the age, and Gaozu praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were crushed he was made Left Assistant on the Yizhou field staff, spoke often on the affairs of the day, and Gaozu welcomed his counsel.

sentences.zh: 終韶州刺史。

translations.literal: He ended as prefect of Shao.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as prefect of Shao.

sentences.zh: 承嗣既還，擢尚輦奉禦，襲周國公，遷秘書監、禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Once Chengsi was restored he was promoted to Imperial Carriage Attendant, inherited Duke of Zhou state, and moved to Director of the Secretariat and Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After Chengsi was restored he became Imperial Carriage Attendant, inherited the dukedom of Zhou, and rose to Director of the Secretariat and Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 俄以太常卿同中書門下三品，未幾辭位。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Minister of Ceremonies with concurrent status as Third Grade at the Central Secretariat and Chancellery; before long he resigned his post.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Minister of Ceremonies with concurrent chancellor rank, but resigned before long.

sentences.zh: 垂拱初，以春官尚書同鳳閣鸞臺平章事，改納言，代蘇良嗣為文昌左相。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chuigong he was Minister of the Directorate of Personnel with concurrent Phoenix Pavilion and Phoenix Terrace Associate Director of Affairs, changed to Supplicator, and replaced Su Liangsi as Left Chancellor of Wenchang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chuigong he was Minister of Personnel with concurrent chancellor status at the Phoenix offices, then made Supplicator and Left Chancellor of Wenchang in Su Liangsi's place.

sentences.zh: 性暴輕忍禍，聞左司郎中喬知之婢窈娘美，且善歌，奪取之，知之作《綠珠篇》以諷，婢得詩恨死。

translations.literal: By nature he was violent, treated lightly the harm he caused others, heard that Left Bureau Director Qiao Zhi's maid Yaoniang was beautiful and skilled in song, seized her; Zhi wrote the "Green Pearl" piece to satirize him, and the maid, receiving the poem, died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: Violent by nature and heedless of the harm he did, he heard that Qiao Zhi's maid Yaoniang was beautiful and sang well, and took her by force; Zhi wrote the "Green Pearl" poem in rebuke, and the maid, on reading it, died of shame and grief.

sentences.zh: 承嗣怒，告酷吏殺之，殘其家。

translations.literal: Chengsi was enraged, reported him to the harsh officials to have him killed, and ravaged his household.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi in rage denounced him to the harsh officials, had him killed, and destroyed his family.

sentences.zh: 初，后擅政，中宗幽逐，承嗣自謂傳國及己，武氏當有天下，即諷后革命，去唐家子孫，誅大臣不附者，倡議追王先世，立宗廟。

translations.literal: At first when the empress monopolized government and Zhongzong was secluded and banished, Chengsi considered that the transmission of the realm would reach himself, that the Wu clan ought to possess the realm; he therefore admonished the empress to change the dynasty, remove the Tang family's descendants, execute great ministers who did not attach themselves, and initiate the proposal to ennoble former generations and establish ancestral temples.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress first seized power and Zhongzong was deposed, Chengsi believed the throne would pass to him and that the Wu should rule the realm; he urged her to change the dynasty, purge the Tang line, kill uncooperative ministers, and ennoble the Wu ancestors and build their temples.

sentences.zh: 又王元慶曰梁王，謚憲；

translations.literal: He further ennobled Yuangqing as Prince of Liang, posthumous title Xian;
translations.idiomatic: He made Yuangqing Prince of Liang, posthumous name Xian;

sentences.zh: 元爽魏王，謚德；

translations.literal: Yuanshuang as Prince of Wei, posthumous title De;
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshuang Prince of Wei, posthumous name De;

sentences.zh: 后從父士讓楚王，謚僖；

translations.literal: the empress's father's younger cousin Shirang as Prince of Chu, posthumous title Xi;
translations.idiomatic: the empress's cousin Shirang Prince of Chu, posthumous name Xi;

sentences.zh: 士逸蜀王，謚節。

translations.literal: Shiyi as Prince of Shu, posthumous title Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyi Prince of Shu, posthumous name Jie.

sentences.zh: 又贈兄子承業陳王。

translations.literal: He further enfeoffed his elder brother's son Chengye as Prince of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: He also made his brother's son Chengye Prince of Chen.

sentences.zh: 而承嗣為魏王，元慶子三思為梁王，士讓之孫攸寧為建昌王、攸歸九江王、攸望會稽王，士逸孫懿宗河內王、嗣宗臨川王、仁範河間王，仁範子載德潁川王，士棱孫攸暨千乘王，惟良子攸宜建安王、攸緒安平王、從子攸止恒安王、重規高平王，承嗣子延基南陽王、延秀淮陽王，三思子崇訓高陽王、崇烈新安王，承業子延暉嗣陳王、延祚鹹安王。

translations.literal: Chengsi himself was Prince of Wei; Yuangqing's son Sansi was Prince of Liang; Shirang's grandsons Youning was Prince of Jianchang, Yougui Prince of Jiujiang, and Youwang Prince of Kuaiji; Shiyi's grandsons Yizong Prince of Henei, Sizong Prince of Linchuan, and Renfan Prince of Hejian; Renfan's son Zaide Prince of Yingchuan; Shileng's grandson Youji Prince of Qiansheng; Weiliang's sons Youyi Prince of Jian'an and Youxu Prince of Anping, his younger cousin's son Youzhi Prince of Heng'an, and Chonggui Prince of Gaoping; Chengsi's sons Yanji Prince of Nanyang and Yanxiu Prince of Huaiyang; Sansi's sons Chongxun Prince of Gaoyang and Chonglie Prince of Xin'an; and Chengye's sons Yanhui heir to Chen and Yanzuo Prince of Xian'an.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi was made Prince of Wei; Yuangqing's son Sansi Prince of Liang; Shirang's grandsons Youning of Jianchang, Yougui of Jiujiang, and Youwang of Kuaiji; Shiyi's grandsons Yizong of Henei, Sizong of Linchuan, and Renfan of Hejian; Renfan's son Zaide of Yingchuan; Shileng's grandson Youji of Qiansheng; Weiliang's sons Youyi of Jian'an and Youxu of Anping, his cousin's son Youzhi of Heng'an, and Chonggui of Gaoping; Chengsi's sons Yanji of Nanyang and Yanxiu of Huaiyang; Sansi's sons Chongxun of Gaoyang and Chonglie of Xin'an; and Chengye's sons Yanhui as heir of Chen and Yanzuo of Xian'an.

sentences.zh: 承嗣實封千戶，監脩國史。

translations.literal: Chengsi had a substantive fief of a thousand households and supervised the compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chengsi held a substantive fief of one thousand households and oversaw the compilation of the national history.

sentences.zh: 密諭后黨鳳閣舍人張嘉福，使洛州人上書請立己為皇太子，以觀后意。

translations.literal: He secretly instructed the empress's partisan, Fengge Attendant Zhang Jiafu, to have men of Luozhou submit a memorial asking that he himself be made crown prince, to gauge the empress's intention.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly directed Zhang Jiafu, a Fengge attendant and ally of Empress Wu, to have Luozhou natives petition that he be made crown prince so as to test the empress's mind.

sentences.zh: 后問岑長倩、格輔元，皆執不宜。

translations.literal: The empress asked Cen Changqian and Ge Fuyuan; both held firmly that it was inappropriate.
translations.idiomatic: The empress consulted Cen Changqian and Ge Fuyuan; both insisted it would be improper.

sentences.zh: 承嗣不得已，奏請責諭嘉福等，不罪也。

translations.literal: Chengsi had no choice but to memorialize requesting reprimand and admonition for Jiafu and the rest, without punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi was forced to petition that Jiafu and the others be rebuked and warned, but not punished.

sentences.zh: 怨長倩等，皆以罪誅。

translations.literal: He resented Changqian and the rest and had them all executed on criminal charges.
translations.idiomatic: Bearing a grudge against Changqian and his colleagues, he had them all put to death on trumped-up charges.

sentences.zh: 以特進罷。

translations.literal: He was dismissed with the title of Special Advancement.
translations.idiomatic: He was removed from office while retaining the honorary rank of Special Advancement.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復同鳳閣鸞臺三品。

translations.literal: Before long he again became Third Rank of Tong Fengge Luantai.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was again made a third-rank minister of the combined secretariat and chancellery.

sentences.zh: 承嗣為左相，而攸寧為納言，故皆罷。

translations.literal: Because Chengsi was Left Chancellor and Youning was Chief Minister, both were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Since Chengsi served as Left Chancellor while Wu Youning held the post of Chief Minister, both were removed.

sentences.zh: 又與三思同三品，不及月俱免，復拜特進。

translations.literal: Again he held third rank together with Sansi; before a month had passed both were dismissed, and he was again appointed Special Advancement.
translations.idiomatic: He and Wu Sansi again shared third rank, but within less than a month both were removed, and Chengsi was reappointed Special Advancement.

sentences.zh: 后決意還太子矣。

translations.literal: The empress had decided to restore the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu had firmly resolved to restore the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷太子太保，不得誌，鞅鞅憤死，贈太尉、并州牧，謚曰宣。

translations.literal: After a long time he was transferred to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent; unable to achieve his aims, he died resentful and discontented; posthumously he was given Grand Commandant and Governor of Bing Prefecture, with the posthumous title Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent; frustrated in his ambitions, he died embittered; he was posthumously made Grand Commandant and military governor of Bing, with the posthumous name Xuan.

sentences.zh: 延基襲爵，后嫌斥其名，更曰繼魏王。

translations.literal: Yanji inherited the title; the empress disliked and rejected his name and changed it to Ji Weiwang ("Successor to the Prince of Wei").
translations.idiomatic: Yanji succeeded to the title, but the empress disliked his name and changed it to "Successor to the Prince of Wei."

sentences.zh: 長安初，與妻永泰郡主及邵王私語張易之兄弟事，后忿爭，語聞，后怒，令自殺，以延義代王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chang'an, he privately discussed the Zhang Yizhi brothers with his wife, the Princess of Yongtai commandery, and Prince Shao; the empress quarreled angrily; when the words were reported the empress was enraged and ordered him to kill himself, and Yanyi replaced him as prince.
translations.idiomatic: In early Chang'an he privately spoke with his wife, the Princess of Yongtai, and Prince Shao about the Zhang Yizhi brothers; the empress flew into a rage when she heard of it, ordered him to take his own life, and had Yanyi succeed as prince.

sentences.zh: 中宗復位，侍中敬暉等言諸武不當王，與君臣白奏：「事不兩大，武家諸王宜皆免。」

translations.literal: When Zhongzong was restored, Attendant-in-Chief Jing Hui and others said the various Wu should not be princes; with the court they plainly memorialized: "Two great powers cannot stand together—the Wu princes should all be removed.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong was restored to the throne, the Attendant-in-Chief Jing Hui and others argued that the Wu princes should not hold royal titles; they joined the ministers in an open memorial: "Two supreme powers cannot coexist—all Wu princes should be stripped of their ranks.

sentences.zh: 帝柔昏不斷，又素畏太后，且欲悅安之，更言攸暨、三思皆與去二張功，以折暉等，才降封一級：三思王德靜郡，攸暨壽春，懿宗為耿國公，攸寧江國，攸望葉國，嗣宗管國，攸宜息國，重規鄶國，延義魏國，攸緒巢國，崇訓酆國，延祿為鹹安郡公。

translations.literal: The emperor was soft and muddled and indecisive; he had always feared the dowager empress; moreover he wished to please Empress Wei and further said Youji and Sansi both had merit in removing the two Zhangs, to counter Hui and the rest, and only reduced their enfeoffments by one rank: Sansi was Prince of Dejing commandery, Youji of Shouchun, Yizong Duke of Geng state, Youning of Jiang state, Youwang of Ye state, Sizong of Guan state, Youyi of Xi state, Chonggui of Zheng state, Yanyi of Wei state, Youxu of Chao state, Chongxun of Feng state, and Yanlu was made Duke of Xian'an commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong was weak, irresolute, and had long feared the dowager; wishing also to please Empress Wei, he replied that Wu Youji and Wu Sansi had shared in the merit of removing the two Zhangs, thereby deflecting Hui and his allies, and reduced their titles by only one rank: Sansi became Prince of Dejing, Youji of Shouchun, Yizong Duke of Geng, Youning of Jiang, Youwang of Ye, Sizong of Guan, Youyi of Xi, Chonggui of Zheng, Yanyi of Wei, Youxu of Chao, Chongxun of Feng, and Yanlu was made Duke of Xian'an.

sentences.zh: 直臣宋務光、蘇安恒上書言：「武諸王饗封，不厭人心。」

translations.literal: Upright ministers Song Wuguang and Su Anheng submitted memorials saying: "The various Wu enjoy enfeoffments and do not satisfy people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: The upright ministers Song Wuguang and Su Anheng memorialized: "The Wu princes still enjoy royal fiefs, and the people remain unsatisfied.

sentences.zh: 帝不悟。

translations.literal: The emperor did not understand.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took no heed.

sentences.zh: 載德終湖州刺史，謚武烈。

translations.literal: Zaide ended as prefect of Huzhou; posthumous title Wulie.
translations.idiomatic: Zaide died as prefect of Huzhou, with the posthumous name Wulie.

sentences.zh: 攸歸歷司屬少卿，至齊州刺史，事母孝，姊亡期，不嘗五辛，語輒流涕。

translations.literal: Yougui served successively as Vice Director of the Bureau of Dependencies, then became prefect of Qi Prefecture; he was filial toward his mother; when his sister's mourning period had not ended he did not taste the five pungent flavors, and when he spoke he would shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: Yougui rose from Vice Director of the Bureau of Dependencies to prefect of Qi; he was devoted to his mother, and while still in mourning for his sister he abstained from the five pungent foods and wept whenever he spoke of her.

sentences.zh: 攸止絳州刺史。

translations.literal: Youzhi was prefect of Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi served as prefect of Jiang.

sentences.zh: 三人死太后時，不及削封。

translations.literal: The three died during the dowager's time and did not suffer reduction of enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: All three died during the dowager's lifetime and escaped reduction of their titles.

sentences.zh: 攸宜歷同州刺史，萬歲通天初，為清邊道行軍大總管。

translations.literal: Youyi successively served as prefect of Tong Prefecture; in the first year of Wansui Tongtian he became Grand Commander of the Qingbian Circuit campaign army.
translations.idiomatic: Youyi served as prefect of Tong, and in the first year of Wansui Tongtian was made grand commander of the Qingbian campaign circuit.

sentences.zh: 討契丹，后親餞白馬寺，師無功還，拜左羽林大將軍。

translations.literal: To campaign against the Khitan, the empress personally saw him off at Baima Temple; the army returned without achievement, and he was appointed General-in-Chief of the Left Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: On a campaign against the Khitans Empress Wu saw him off at Baima Temple; when the army returned without success he was made General-in-Chief of the Left Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 景龍時，遷右羽林，卒。

translations.literal: In the Jinglong era he was transferred to the Right Palace Guard and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jinglong era he was transferred to the Right Palace Guard, then died.

sentences.zh: 總禁兵前後十年。

translations.literal: He commanded the forbidden troops for ten years in all.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded the palace guards for ten years in all.

sentences.zh: 嗣宗終司衛卿。

translations.literal: Sizong ended as Director of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Sizong ended his career as Director of the Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 重規為汴、鄭二州刺史，未至，役人營繕，后怒，貶廬州刺史。

translations.literal: Chonggui was made prefect of Bian and Zheng prefectures; before he arrived, corvée laborers were set to build and repair; the empress was angry and demoted him to prefect of Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chonggui was appointed prefect of Bian and Zheng but, before taking up office, had laborers put to work on his quarters; the empress was enraged and demoted him to prefect of Lu.

sentences.zh: 自是著令：諸王為州，不得擅營治。

translations.literal: From this an order was written: princes serving as prefects might not on their own authority construct or maintain estates.
translations.idiomatic: From this a regulation was issued: princes assigned to prefectures might not undertake private construction on their own authority.

sentences.zh: 突厥之叛，以重規為天兵中道大總管，與沙咤忠義、張仁亶引眾三十萬討之。

translations.literal: When the Turks rebelled, Chonggui was made Grand Commander of the Central Tianbing Circuit, and with Shatuo Zhongyi and Zhang Renbian led an army of three hundred thousand to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks rebelled, Chonggui was appointed grand commander of the central Tianbing circuit and, with Shatuo Zhongyi and Zhang Renbian, led three hundred thousand men against them.

sentences.zh: 左羽林大將軍閻敬容為西道後軍，兵十五萬後援。

translations.literal: General-in-Chief of the Left Palace Guard Yan Rongrong was rear army on the western route, with one hundred fifty thousand troops as rear support.
translations.idiomatic: General Yan Rongrong of the Left Palace Guard commanded the western rear corps with one hundred fifty thousand men in support.

sentences.zh: 還為左金吾衛大將軍，終衛尉卿。

translations.literal: On return he became General-in-Chief of the Left Golden Crow Guard and ended as Director of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he became General-in-Chief of the Left Golden Crow Guard and ended as Director of the Guards.

sentences.zh: 延秀母本帶方人，坐其家沒入奚官，以姝惠，賜承嗣，生延秀。

translations.literal: Yanxiu's mother was originally from Daifang; because of her family she was confiscated into the palace service for non-Han women; because of her beautiful grace she was granted to Chengsi, and bore Yanxiu.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxiu's mother was a native of Daifang; her family was confiscated and she was enrolled in the palace service for foreign women; for her beauty she was given to Chengsi, who fathered Yanxiu.

sentences.zh: 突厥默啜薦女和親，后令延秀納之，詔右豹韜大將軍閻知微、右武衛郎將楊鸞莊賫金幣送至突厥所。

translations.literal: The Türk Mochuo offered his daughter for a marriage alliance; the empress ordered Yanxiu to marry her and decreed that Right General of the Leopard Bow Guard Yan Zhiwei and Right Militant Guard Commander Yang Luanzhuang take gold and silks to deliver to the Türk encampment.
translations.idiomatic: The Türk khan Mochuo offered his daughter for alliance marriage; the empress ordered Yanxiu to marry her and sent Right General Yan Zhiwei and Commander Yang Luanzhuang with gold and silks to the Türk court.

sentences.zh: 知微等潛約默啜執延秀進寇媯、檀，故延秀不得歸。

translations.literal: Zhiwei and the rest secretly agreed with Mochuo to seize Yanxiu and advance to raid Guizhou and Tanzhou, so Yanxiu could not return.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiwei and his party secretly agreed with Mochuo to detain Yanxiu and invade Guizhou and Tanzhou, and Yanxiu was unable to return.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，默啜請和，因延秀送款，還，封柏國公，左衛中郎將。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shenlong, Mochuo requested peace and, through Yanxiu, sent pledges of allegiance; on his return Yanxiu was enfeoffed Duke of Bo state and made Central Commander of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In early Shenlong, Mochuo sought peace and, through Yanxiu, sent terms of submission; Yanxiu returned, was made Duke of Bo, and appointed Central Commander of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 宗兄崇訓尚安樂公主，數與宴昵，頗通突厥語。

translations.literal: His clansman elder brother Chongxun married Princess Anle; he often banqueted intimately with her and was quite versed in Türk speech.
translations.idiomatic: His kinsman Chongxun had married Princess Anle; he often feasted with her in intimacy and knew considerable Türkish.

sentences.zh: 仿虜謳舞，姿度閑冶，主愛悅。

translations.literal: He imitated barbarian songs and dances; his bearing was easy and alluring; the princess loved and delighted in him.
translations.idiomatic: He mimicked barbarian songs and dances with an easy, alluring manner, and the princess was captivated.

sentences.zh: 會崇訓死，遂私侍主，后因尚焉。

translations.literal: When Chongxun died he then privately attended the princess; afterward because of this he was married to her.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongxun died he secretly served the princess as her lover; later the empress formally approved their marriage.

sentences.zh: 以太常卿兼右衛將軍，封恒國公。

translations.literal: He was made Director of Ceremonies with concurrent General of the Right Guard and enfeoffed Duke of Heng state.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Director of Ceremonies with concurrent command of the Right Guard and enfeoffed as Duke of Heng.

sentences.zh: 三思死，韋后復私延秀，故延秀益自肆。

translations.literal: When Sansi died, Empress Wei again privately took Yanxiu, so Yanxiu grew ever more unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: After Sansi's death Empress Wei again took Yanxiu as her lover, and he grew ever more brazen.

sentences.zh: 主府倉曹參軍何鳳說曰：「今天下系心武家，庶幾再興。

translations.literal: A staff member of the princess's household, Warehouse Clerk He Feng, urged him: "Now the realm's hearts are bound to the Wu clan; perhaps it may rise again.
translations.idiomatic: He Feng, a warehouse clerk on the princess's staff, told him: "All hearts in the empire still cling to the Wu house; they may yet rise again.

sentences.zh: 且讖曰『黑衣神孫被天裳』，神孫非公尚誰哉？」

translations.literal: Moreover a prophecy says "The divine grandson in black robes receives Heaven's garment"—if not you, who is the divine grandson?"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover a prophecy runs, "The divine grandson in black robes receives Heaven's garment"—if the divine grandson is not you, who can it be?"

sentences.zh: 因勸服阜衣惑眾。

translations.literal: He therefore urged wearing dark robes to bewitch the masses.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore urged him to wear dark clothing and delude the crowd.

sentences.zh: 韋后敗，尚與主居禁中，同斬肅章門。

translations.literal: When Empress Wei was defeated, he was still dwelling with the princess inside the forbidden precincts; both were beheaded together at Su Zhang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wei fell, he was still living with the princess inside the palace; both were executed together at Su Zhang Gate.

sentences.zh: 攸望以太府卿貶死春州。

translations.literal: Youwang, from his post as Director of the Palace Storehouses, was demoted and died in Chun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Youwang, serving as Director of the Palace Storehouses, was demoted and died in Chun.

sentences.zh: 諸武屬坐延秀誅徙者略盡，獨載德子平一以文章顯，與攸緒常避盛滿，故免，自有傳。

translations.literal: The various Wu dependents implicated in Yanxiu's case and executed or exiled were nearly all gone; only Zaide's son Pingyi distinguished himself through literature, and with Youxu he always avoided the height of fullness, and so escaped punishment—each has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Nearly all Wu dependents implicated through Yanxiu were executed or banished; only Zaide's son Pingyi won renown for his writing, and with Youxu he habitually shunned the peak of power and so was spared—each has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 攸寧，天授中擢累納言。

translations.literal: Youning—in the Tianshou era he was repeatedly promoted to Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Youning—in the Tianshou era he rose through repeated promotions to Chief Minister.

sentences.zh: 逾年，以左羽林衛大將軍罷，俄還納言。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was dismissed as General-in-Chief of the Left Palace Guard; soon he returned as Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was removed as General-in-Chief of the Left Palace Guard; soon he returned as Chief Minister.

sentences.zh: 久乃罷為冬官尚書。

translations.literal: After a long time he was dismissed and made Minister of Public Works.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was dismissed and made Minister of Public Works.

sentences.zh: 聖歷初，同鳳閣鸞臺平章事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shenli he became Associate Director of Tong Fengge Luantai.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shenli he became associate director of the combined secretariat and chancellery.

sentences.zh: 自承嗣、三思罷政事，間一年，攸寧、三思復當國，置句使，苛取民貲產，毀族者凡十七八，呼天自冤。

translations.literal: From the time Chengsi and Sansi were removed from government affairs, with an interval of one year Youning and Sansi again held the state, established extracting envoys, harshly seized the goods and property of the people, and families destroyed numbered seventeen or eighteen in all—cries to Heaven in self-proclaimed injustice.
translations.idiomatic: A year after Chengsi and Sansi left office, Youning and Sansi again dominated government, appointed extraction agents, and ruthlessly seized people's property; seventeen or eighteen clans were ruined, crying to Heaven of their injustice.

sentences.zh: 築大庫百餘舍聚所得財，一昔火，不遺一錢。

translations.literal: They built great storehouses of more than a hundred chambers to gather the wealth obtained; in one night fire consumed it, not leaving a single coin.
translations.idiomatic: They built more than a hundred storehouse chambers for their takings; one night it all burned, not a coin left.

sentences.zh: 以冬官尚書罷。

translations.literal: He was dismissed as Minister of Public Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was removed as Minister of Public Works.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，終岐州刺史，贈尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In early Shenlong he ended as prefect of Qi Prefecture and was posthumously given Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In early Shenlong he died as prefect of Qi and was posthumously made Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 三思當太后時，累進夏官、春官尚書，監脩國史，爵為王。

translations.literal: When Sansi was in power under the dowager he was repeatedly advanced to Minister of War and Minister of Rites, supervised compilation of the national history, and held princely rank.
translations.idiomatic: While Wu Sansi held power under the dowager he rose repeatedly to Minister of War and Minister of Rites, supervised the national history, and held princely rank.

sentences.zh: 契丹陷營州，以榆關道安撫大使屯邊。

translations.literal: When the Khitan captured Ying Prefecture, he was made Pacification Commissioner of the Yuguan Circuit and stationed on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitans captured Yingzhou he was made pacification commissioner of the Yuguan circuit and stationed on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 還，同鳳閣鸞臺三品，逾月去位。

translations.literal: On return he became Third Rank of Tong Fengge Luantai; after more than a month he left office.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he became a third-rank minister of the secretariat and chancellery; after more than a month he left office.

sentences.zh: 又檢校內史，罷為太子少保，遷賓客，仍監國史。

translations.literal: Again he was acting Director of the Palace Secretariat; dismissed as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, transferred as Guest of the Heir Apparent, and still supervised the national history.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as acting director of the Palace Secretariat; removed as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, transferred as guest of the heir apparent, and still supervised the national history.

sentences.zh: 三思性傾諛，善迎諧主意，鉤探隱微，故后頗信任，數幸其第，賞予尤渥。

translations.literal: Sansi by nature inclined to flattery; he was skilled at welcoming and harmonizing with the sovereign's intent, hooking and probing hidden matters, so the empress quite trusted him, often visited his residence, and rewards were especially generous.
translations.idiomatic: Sansi was by nature a flatterer; skilled at reading and matching the sovereign's wishes and at probing hidden matters, he won the empress's deep trust, was often received at his residence, and received especially lavish rewards.

sentences.zh: 薛、二張方烝蠱，三思痛屈節，為懷義禦馬，倡言昌宗為王子晉後身，引公卿歌詠淫汙，然媚人而不恥也。

translations.literal: When Xue Huaiyi and the two Zhangs were dominating with debauchery, Sansi painfully bent his integrity—he held Huaiyi's horse reins, proclaimed Changzong was the reincarnation of Prince Zixu, led high ministers in singing licentious verses—yet he flattered without shame.
translations.idiomatic: While Xue Huaiyi and the two Zhangs held sway with their debauchery, Sansi humiliated himself without limit—he held Huaiyi's horse, declared Changzong the reincarnation of Prince Zixu, and led the high ministers in singing licentious verses—yet he fawned without shame.

sentences.zh: 后春秋高，厭居宮中，三思欲因此市權，誘脅群不肖，即建營三陽宮於嵩山、興泰宮於萬壽山，請太后歲臨幸，己與二張扈侍馳騁，竊威福自私雲。

translations.literal: The empress's years were advanced and she tired of dwelling in the palace; Sansi wished by this to trade for power, enticed and coerced the unworthy, immediately built and campaigned the Three Yang Palace on Mount Song and the Xingtai Palace on Mount Wanshou, requested the dowager's annual visits, himself and the two Zhangs attending in escort racing about, secretly stealing authority and blessings for private ends.
translations.idiomatic: As the empress grew old she tired of life within the palace; Sansi sought to turn this to power, lured and coerced the worthless, built the Three Yang Palace on Mount Song and the Xingtai Palace on Mount Wanshou, urged the dowager to visit each year, and with the two Zhangs attended her in reckless outings, stealing authority and favor for himself.

sentences.zh: 工役鉅萬萬，百姓愁嘆。

translations.literal: Corvée laborers numbered in the tens of millions; the common people groaned and lamented.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée labor ran into the tens of millions; the people groaned in misery.

sentences.zh: 崇訓之尚主也，三思方輔政，中宗居東宮，欲寵耀其下，乃令具親迎禮。

translations.literal: When Chongxun married the princess, Sansi was just assisting in government; Zhongzong dwelt in the Eastern Palace; wishing to display favor and glory to his followers, he ordered full ceremony for receiving the bride.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongxun married the princess, Sansi was just in power and Zhongzong still lived in the Eastern Palace; wishing to show favor to his followers, he ordered the full ceremony for receiving the bride.

sentences.zh: 宰相李嶠、蘇味道等及沈佺期、宋之問諸有名士，造作文辭，慢泄相矜，無復禮法。

translations.literal: Chancellors Li Jiao, Su Weidao, and others, and famous men such as Shen Quanqi and Song Zhiwen composed literary pieces; slowly they leaked and boasted to one another, without regard for ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellors Li Jiao and Su Weidao and famous writers such as Shen Quanqi and Song Zhiwen composed literary pieces; they leaked drafts and boasted to one another, with no regard for propriety.

sentences.zh: 中宗復位，擢崇訓駙馬都尉、太常卿，兼左衛將軍。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong was restored he promoted Chongxun to Commandant-Equerry, Director of Ceremonies, with concurrent General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong was restored he promoted Chongxun to Commandant-Equerry and Director of Ceremonies with concurrent command of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 三思進位司空、同中書門下三品，加實戶五百。

translations.literal: Sansi advanced to Minister of Works, Third Rank of Tong Zhongshu Menxia, with an added substantive fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Sansi was advanced to Minister of Works and third-rank chancellor, with an added substantive fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 固辭，進開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He firmly declined; he was advanced to Acting-Esteemed Equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined; he was advanced to Acting-Esteemed Equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 會降封，裁減實戶。

translations.literal: When enfeoffments were reduced he only trimmed the substantive households.
translations.idiomatic: When titles were reduced he only trimmed the substantive households.

sentences.zh: 俄以太后遺詔還所減，而封崇訓鎬國公。

translations.literal: Soon by the dowager's testamentary edict what had been reduced was restored, and Chongxun was enfeoffed Duke of Hao state.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, by the dowager's testamentary edict, what had been reduced was restored, and Chongxun was enfeoffed Duke of Hao.

sentences.zh: 初，桓彥範等已誅二張，薛季昶、劉幽求勸並誅三思等，不從。

translations.literal: At first Huan Yanfan and the rest had already executed the two Zhangs; Xue Jichang and Liu Youqiu urged executing Sansi and the rest together; they were not followed.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Yanfan and his allies had already executed the two Zhangs; Xue Jichang and Liu Youqiu urged that Sansi and his party be killed as well, but were not heeded.

sentences.zh: 翌日，三思因韋后潛入宮中，反易國政，數日而彥範等皆失柄，所斥去者悉還。

translations.literal: The next day Sansi, through Empress Wei, secretly entered the palace and reversed national policy; within several days Yanfan and the rest all lost their handles of power, and those who had been dismissed all returned.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Sansi entered the palace secretly through Empress Wei and reversed state policy; within days Yanfan and his allies lost their power, and those who had been dismissed all returned.

sentences.zh: 詔群臣復循太后法。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the court ministers again to follow the dowager's laws.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the court to follow the dowager's laws again.

sentences.zh: 三思建言：「大帝封泰山，則天皇后建明堂，封嵩山，二聖之美不可廢。」

translations.literal: Sansi submitted advice: "The Great Emperor enfeoffed Mount Tai; Empress Zetian built the Bright Hall and enfeoffed Mount Song—the beauty of the two sages cannot be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Sansi submitted advice: "The Great Emperor performed the feng on Mount Tai; Empress Zetian built the Bright Hall and performed the feng on Mount Song—the glory of the two sages must not be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 帝韙其言，遂更名五縣曰乾封、合宮、永昌、登封、告成雲。

translations.literal: The emperor assented to his words and thus renamed five counties to Qianfeng, Hegong, Yongchang, Dengfeng, and Gaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his words and renamed five counties Qianfeng, Hegong, Yongchang, Dengfeng, and Gaocheng.

sentences.zh: 明年春，大旱，帝遣三思、攸暨禱乾陵而雨，帝悅。

translations.literal: The next year in spring there was great drought; the emperor sent Sansi and Youji to pray at Qianling and rain came; the emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The next spring a great drought struck; the emperor sent Sansi and Youji to pray at Qianling, rain followed, and the emperor was pleased.

sentences.zh: 三思因主請復崇恩廟，昊、順二陵，皆置令丞。

translations.literal: Sansi through the princess requested restoration of the Chong'en Temple, the Wu and Shun two mausoleums, all with directors and assistants appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Through the princess, Sansi requested restoration of the Chong'en Temple and the Wu and Shun mausoleums, each with appointed directors and assistants.

sentences.zh: 其黨鄭愔上《聖感頌》，帝為刻石。

translations.literal: His partisan Zheng Yin submitted "Ode on Sagely Responsiveness"; the emperor had it carved in stone.
translations.idiomatic: His partisan Zheng Yin submitted the "Ode on Sagely Responsiveness," and the emperor had it carved in stone.

sentences.zh: 補闕張景源建言：「母子承業，不可言中興，所下制書皆除之。」

translations.literal: Remonstrance Official Zhang Jingyuan submitted advice: "Mother and son inherit the enterprise—it cannot be called restoration; all issued regulations using that term should be removed.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Official Zhang Jingyuan submitted advice: "Mother and son together inherit the enterprise—this cannot be called restoration; all edicts using that term should be struck out.

sentences.zh: 於是天下名祠改唐興、龍興雲。

translations.literal: Thereupon famous temples throughout the realm were changed to Tangxing and Longxing.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon famous temples throughout the realm were renamed Tangxing and Longxing.

sentences.zh: 補闕權若訥又言：「制詔如貞觀故事。

translations.literal: Remonstrance Official Quan Ruone again said: "Regulations and edicts should follow the Zhenguan precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Official Quan Ruone again said: "Edicts and regulations should follow the Zhenguan precedent.

sentences.zh: 且太后遺訓，母儀也；

translations.literal: Moreover the dowager's testamentary instructions are the model of motherhood;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the dowager's testamentary instructions are the model of motherhood;

sentences.zh: 太宗舊章，祖德也。

translations.literal: Taizong's old statutes are the virtue of the ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong's old statutes are the virtue of the ancestors.

sentences.zh: 沿襲當自近者始。」

translations.literal: In following precedent one should begin with what is near.
translations.idiomatic: In following precedent one should begin with what is nearest.

sentences.zh: 帝褒答。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and replied.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him and replied.

sentences.zh: 是時，起球場苑中，詔文武三品分朋為都，帝與皇后臨觀。

translations.literal: At this time a ball ground was raised within the park; an edict ordered civil and military officials of third rank to divide into teams as directorates; the emperor and empress observed in person.
translations.idiomatic: At this time a ball ground was built within the park; an edict ordered civil and military officials of third rank to divide into teams; the emperor and empress watched in person.

sentences.zh: 崇訓與駙馬都尉楊慎交註膏築場，以利其澤，用功不訾，人苦之。

translations.literal: Chongxun and Commandant-Equerry Yang Shenjiao applied grease to build the ground, to profit their emoluments; labor expended was beyond reckoning; people suffered bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: Chongxun and Commandant-Equerry Yang Shenjiao smeared the ground with grease to enrich themselves; the labor was beyond reckoning, and the people suffered bitterly.

sentences.zh: 三思既私韋后，又與上官昭容亂，內忌節湣太子，即與主謀廢之。

translations.literal: Sansi, having privately taken Empress Wei, also had illicit relations with Shangguan Zhaorong; inwardly he resented the Reverent and Mournful Crown Prince and immediately joined the princess in plotting to depose him.
translations.idiomatic: Sansi, who had taken Empress Wei as his lover, also had an affair with Shangguan Zhaorong; inwardly he resented the Reverent and Mournful Crown Prince and joined the princess in plotting to depose him.

sentences.zh: 太子懼，故發羽林兵圍三思第，並崇訓斬之，殺其黨十餘人。

translations.literal: The crown prince feared this and therefore sent Palace Guard troops to besiege Sansi's residence; both he and Chongxun were beheaded, and more than ten of their partisans were killed.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince, in fear, sent palace guard troops to besiege Sansi's residence; both Sansi and Chongxun were beheaded, and more than ten of their partisans were killed.

sentences.zh: 時疾三思奸亂竊國，比司馬懿。

translations.literal: At the time people detested Sansi's treacherous disorder in stealing the state, comparing him to Sima Yi.
translations.idiomatic: At the time people detested Sansi's treacherous seizure of power and compared him to Sima Yi.

sentences.zh: 其忌阻正人特甚，嘗曰：「我不知何等名善人，唯與我者殆是哉。」

translations.literal: He especially feared and obstructed upright men; he once said: "I do not know what sort are called good men—only those with me are perhaps such.
translations.idiomatic: He especially feared and obstructed upright men; he once said, "I do not know what sort of men are called good—only those on my side are perhaps good.

sentences.zh: 與宗楚客兄弟、紀處訥、崔湜、甘元柬相驅煽，王同皎、周憬、張仲之等不勝憤，謀殺之，為冉祖雍、宋之愻、李悛所白，皆坐死。

translations.literal: He drove and fanned together with the Zong Chuke brothers, Ji Chuna, Cui Shi, and Gan Yuanjian; Wang Tongjiao, Zhou Jing, Zhang Zhongzhi and others could not contain their rage and plotted to kill him; they were reported by Ran Zuyong, Song Zhixun, and Li Jun—all were punished with death.
translations.idiomatic: He drove affairs together with the Zong Chuke brothers, Ji Chuna, Cui Shi, and Gan Yuanjian; Wang Tongjiao, Zhou Jing, Zhang Zhongzhi, and others, unable to contain their rage, plotted to kill him; they were denounced by Ran Zuyong, Song Zhixun, and Li Jun—all were put to death.

sentences.zh: 因逮染五王，而崔湜遣周利貞就殺之，故祖雍與御史姚紹之等五人，號「三思五狗」。

translations.literal: They were implicated in dragging in the five princes, and Cui Shi sent Zhou Lizhen to go kill them; therefore Zuyong with Censor Yao Shaozhi and four others were called "Sansi's Five Dogs."
translations.idiomatic: They were implicated in dragging down the five princes, and Cui Shi sent Zhou Lizhen to kill them; therefore Zuyong, Censor Yao Shaozhi, and three others were called "Sansi's Five Dogs."

sentences.zh: 司農少卿趙履溫、中書舍人鄭愔、長安令馬構、司勛郎中崔日用、監察御史李𢘽托其權，熏炙內外，其尤幹政事者，天下語曰：「崔、冉、鄭，亂時政。」

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Chamberlain of Agriculture Zhao Luwen, Secretariat Draftsman Zheng Yin, Prefect of Chang'an Ma Gou, Bureau of Merit Director Cui Riyong, and Investigating Censor Li Jun relied on his power, fumed and scorched inside and outside; among those especially involved in government affairs the realm said: "Cui, Ran, and Zheng disorder the times and government.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Chamberlain of Agriculture Zhao Luwen, Secretariat Draftsman Zheng Yin, Prefect of Chang'an Ma Gou, Bureau of Merit Director Cui Riyong, and Investigating Censor Li Jun relied on his power and scorched court and country; among those most active in government affairs people said, "Cui, Ran, and Zheng disorder the times.

sentences.zh: 以爵賞自相崇樹，凡構大獄，汙點善良，破壞其宗，天下為蕩然。

translations.literal: They honored and elevated one another with titles and rewards; whenever they constructed great cases they stained and defamed the good, destroyed their clans—the realm was left in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: They honored one another with titles and rewards; whenever they engineered great cases they stained the good and destroyed whole clans, until the realm was in turmoil.

sentences.zh: 始韋月將、高軫上疏，極言三思過惡，有司殺月將，逐軫惡地。

translations.literal: At first Wei Yuejiang and Gao Zhen submitted memorials vigorously stating Sansi's transgressions and evils; the authorities killed Yuejiang and exiled Zhen to a vicious region.
translations.idiomatic: At first Wei Yuejiang and Gao Zhen memorialized at length on Sansi's crimes; the authorities killed Yuejiang and exiled Zhen to a remote, harsh region.

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎宋璟執奏，俄見斥。

translations.literal: Yellow Gate Vice Director Song Jing firmly memorialized; soon he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Gate Vice Director Song Jing submitted a forceful memorial; soon he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 其權大抵如此。

translations.literal: His power was broadly such as this.
translations.idiomatic: His power was broadly of this sort.

sentences.zh: 既死，帝為舉哀，廢朝五日，贈太尉，復封梁王，謚曰宣。

translations.literal: After his death the emperor mourned for him, suspended court for five days, posthumously gave Grand Commandant, restored enfeoffment as Prince of Liang, posthumous title Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: After his death the emperor mourned him, suspended court for five days, posthumously made him Grand Commandant, restored his enfeoffment as Prince of Liang, and gave him the posthumous name Xuan.

sentences.zh: 追封崇訓魯王，謚曰忠。

translations.literal: Chongxun was posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Lu, posthumous title Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Chongxun was posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Lu with the posthumous name Zhong.

sentences.zh: 主以太子首祭三思柩。

translations.literal: The princess used the crown prince's title to make the first offering at Sansi's bier.
translations.idiomatic: The princess had the crown prince make the first offering at Sansi's bier.

sentences.zh: 睿宗立，以父子皆逆節，斫棺暴屍，夷其墓。

translations.literal: When Ruizong took the throne, because father and son had both committed treason, [they] chopped open the coffins and exposed the corpses and razed their tombs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, because Wu Sansi and his son had both committed treason, their coffins were opened, their corpses exposed, and their tombs razed.

sentences.zh: 懿宗以司農卿爵為郡王，歷懷、洛二州刺史。

translations.literal: Yizong on the basis of his rank as Director of the Chamberlain of Agriculture was enfeoffed Prince of a commandery, and served as prefect of Huai and Luo prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yizong was enfeoffed a princely commandery on the strength of his post as Director of the Chamberlain of Agriculture and served as prefect of Huai and Luo.

sentences.zh: 神功元年，孫萬榮敗王孝傑兵，詔懿宗為神兵道大總管討之，而婁師德、沙咤忠義並為總管，兵凡二十萬，次趙州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shenggong, Sun Wanrong defeated Wang Xiaojie's army; an edict made Yizong Grand Commander of the Divine Troops Route to campaign against him, while Lou Shide and Shatuo Zhongyi were both made commanders-in-chief; troops totaled two hundred thousand and halted at Zhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 697 Sun Wanrong routed Wang Xiaojie's army; Yizong was appointed Grand Commander of the Divine Troops Route to suppress him, with Lou Shide and Shatuo Zhongyi as co-commanders. Two hundred thousand troops encamped at Zhao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 懿宗聞賊且至，懼不知所出，欲棄軍走，或勸曰：「賊雖眾，無輜載，以鈔剽為命，若按兵老之，擊其歸，可成大功。」

translations.literal: Yizong heard the rebels were about to arrive, feared and did not know what to do, wished to abandon the army and flee; someone advised: "Though the rebels are numerous, they have no baggage trains and live by raiding and plunder—if you hold the troops and wear them down, striking them on their return, you can achieve great merit.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the rebels were near, Yizong panicked and thought of abandoning the army and fleeing. An adviser said, "Though numerous, they have no supply train and live by raiding. Hold your ground and wear them down, then strike them on the retreat—you can win a great victory.

sentences.zh: 懿宗不暇計，退保相州，賊遂進屠趙州。

translations.literal: Yizong had no time to calculate; he withdrew to defend Xiang Prefecture, and the rebels advanced and slaughtered Zhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yizong had no time for such counsel. He withdrew to Xiang Prefecture, and the rebels advanced and massacred Zhao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 後萬榮死，懿宗復與婁師德撫循河北，人有自賊中歸者，一切抵死，先剔取膽，乃殺之，血沫前，而舉動自如。

translations.literal: Later Wanrong died; Yizong again with Lou Shide pacified and consoled Hebei; anyone who returned from among the rebels was without exception put to death—first the gall was gouged out, then he was killed; blood foamed before him yet his movements were at ease.
translations.idiomatic: After Wanrong's death Yizong again joined Lou Shide in pacifying Hebei. Anyone who returned from rebel territory was put to death without exception—first his gall was cut out, then he was killed. Blood foamed before Yizong's face, yet he moved as calmly as ever.

sentences.zh: 始萬榮入寇也，別帥何阿小陷冀州，殺人無餘種，以懿宗暴忍似之，故號稱「兩何」，相語曰：「唯此兩何，殺人最多。」

translations.literal: When Wanrong first invaded, the separate commander He A'xiao took Jizhou and killed until no seed remained; because Yizong's violence and cruelty resembled his, they were called the "Two Hes"; people said to one another: "Only these two Hes kill the most."
translations.idiomatic: When Wanrong first invaded, his lieutenant He A'xiao seized Jizhou and slaughtered the population to the last. Yizong's savagery matched his, so the two were called the "Two Hes." People said, "Of all killers, only these two Hes are worst."

sentences.zh: 初，懿宗天授間受詔訊大獄，誅大臣王公，皆深排巧引，內刑塹中，無有脫者。

translations.literal: At first, during the Tianshou era Yizong received orders to interrogate great cases and execute great ministers and imperial princes—all were deeply framed with artful entrapment, sent into the execution ditch, and none escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the Tianshou era Yizong had been ordered to interrogate major political cases. He executed ministers and princes through elaborate framing and entrapment; none sent into the execution pit escaped.

sentences.zh: 其險酷雖周、來等不能繼也。

translations.literal: His treachery and cruelty—even Zhou and Lai and the like could not match it.
translations.idiomatic: His treachery and cruelty even Zhou Xingqian and Lai Junchen could not equal.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，遷太子詹事，終懷州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong he was moved to Supervisor of the Crown Prince's Household and ended as prefect of Huai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shenlong era he was made Supervisor of the Crown Prince's Household and ended his career as prefect of Huai.

sentences.zh: 攸暨自右衛中郎將尚太平公主，拜駙馬都尉，累遷右衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Youji from Central Guard Gentlemen-of-the-House married Princess Taiping, was appointed Commandant of Cavalry, and rose repeatedly to Grand General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Youji, a Central Guard captain, married Princess Taiping, was made Commandant of Cavalry, and rose to Grand General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 天授中，自千乘郡王進封定王，實封戶六百。

translations.literal: During Tianshou, from Prince of Qiansheng he advanced to Prince of Ding, with six hundred enfeoffment households in fact.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianshou he advanced from Prince of Qiansheng to Prince of Ding, with six hundred households as his actual fief.

sentences.zh: 遷麟臺監司祀卿。

translations.literal: He was moved to Director of the Lin Terrace and Minister of Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Director of the Lin Terrace and Minister of Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 長安中，降王壽春，加特進。

translations.literal: During Chang'an he was demoted to Prince of Shouchun and given Special Advancement.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chang'an era he was demoted to Prince of Shouchun and granted Special Advancement.

sentences.zh: 中宗時，拜司徒，復王定，加戶千，固辭，進開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Under Zhongzong he was appointed Minister of Works, restored as Prince of Ding with household yield increased by a thousand; he firmly declined and advanced to Pillar of State with credentials equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Zhongzong he was made Minister of Works and restored as Prince of Ding with a thousand additional fief households; he declined firmly and was advanced to Pillar of State with credentials equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 延秀之誅，降楚國公。

translations.literal: When Yanxiu was executed, [Youji] was demoted to Duke of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Yanxiu was executed, Youji was demoted to Duke of Chu.

sentences.zh: 攸暨沈謹和厚，於時無忤，專自奉養而已。

translations.literal: Youji was deep, cautious, and mild; at the time he gave no offense, devoting himself only to self-support.
translations.idiomatic: Youji was grave, cautious, and mild. He gave no offense at court and devoted himself only to his own comfort.

sentences.zh: 景龍中卒，贈太尉、并州大都督，還定王，謚曰忠簡。
