translations.literal: He died during Jinglong, was posthumously given Grand Commandant and Great Governor of Bing Prefecture, restored as Prince of Ding, posthumous title Zhongjian.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Jinglong era and was posthumously made Grand Commandant and Great Governor of Bing, restored as Prince of Ding with the posthumous name Zhongjian.

sentences.zh: 坐公主大逆，夷其墓。

translations.literal: Because of the princess's great treason, his tomb was razed.
translations.idiomatic: When the princess was condemned for great treason, his tomb was razed.

sentences.zh: 韋溫者，中宗廢后庶人從父兄也。

translations.literal: Wei Wen was the deposed Empress Wei's father's younger brother by a cousin line of Zhongzong.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Wen was a cousin on the father's side of Empress Wei, whom Emperor Zhongzong had deposed.

sentences.zh: 后父玄貞，歷普州參軍事，以女為皇太子妃，故擢累豫州刺史。

translations.literal: The empress's father Xuanzhen had served as clerk in Pu Prefecture; because his daughter became the crown prince's consort he was repeatedly promoted to prefect of Yu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's father Wei Xuanzhen had served as a clerk in Pu Prefecture. When his daughter became crown prince's consort he was repeatedly promoted, eventually to prefect of Yu.

sentences.zh: 帝幽廬陵，玄貞流死欽州，妻崔為蠻首寧承所殺，四子洵、浩、洞、泚同死容州，后二女弟逃還京師。

translations.literal: When the emperor was confined at Luling, Xuanzhen died in exile at Qin Prefecture; his wife Cui was killed by the barbarian chieftain Ning Cheng; the four sons Xun, Hao, Dong, and Zhi likewise died at Rong Prefecture; the empress's two younger sisters fled back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was confined at Luling, Xuanzhen died in exile at Qin. His wife Lady Cui was killed by the tribal chieftain Ning Cheng. Their four sons Xun, Hao, Dong, and Zhi likewise perished at Rong. The empress's two younger sisters fled back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝復政，是日詔贈玄貞上洛郡王、太師、雍州牧、益州大都督，溫父玄儼魯國公、特進、并州大都督。

translations.literal: When the emperor resumed rule, that same day an edict posthumously made Xuanzhen Prince of Shangluo, Grand Preceptor, Governor of Yong Prefecture, and Great Governor of Yi Prefecture; Wen's father Xuanyan was made Duke of Lu with Special Advancement and Great Governor of Bing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor resumed power, that same day an edict posthumously enfeoffed Xuanzhen Prince of Shangluo, made him Grand Preceptor, Governor of Yong, and Great Governor of Yi; Wen's father Xuanyan was made Duke of Lu with Special Advancement and Great Governor of Bing.

sentences.zh: 遣使者迎玄貞喪，詔廣州都督周仁軌討寧承，斬其首祭崔柩，官仁軌左羽林大將軍，汝南郡公。

translations.literal: Envoys were sent to fetch Xuanzhen's coffin; the emperor ordered Guangzhou Governor Zhou Rengui to campaign against Ning Cheng, behead him, and offer his head before Cui's bier; Rengui was made Grand General of the Left Feathered Forest and Duke of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were sent to bring back Xuanzhen's remains. The emperor ordered Guangzhou Governor Zhou Rengui to campaign against Ning Cheng, behead him, and offer his head before Lady Cui's coffin. Rengui was made Grand General of the Left Feathered Forest and Duke of Runan.

sentences.zh: 柩至，帝與后登長樂宮望而哭，贈酆王，謚「文獻」，號廟曰「褒德」，陵曰「榮先」，置令丞，給百戶掃除。

translations.literal: When the bier arrived, the emperor and empress climbed Changle Palace to look and weep; he was posthumously made Prince of Feng with posthumous title "Wenxian," the temple called Baode, the tomb Rongxian; stewards and assistants were appointed and a hundred households given for sweeping.
translations.idiomatic: When the coffin arrived the emperor and empress climbed Changle Palace to gaze upon it and weep. Xuanzhen was posthumously made Prince of Feng with the posthumous name Wenxian; his temple was called Baode and his tomb Rongxian. Stewards were appointed and a hundred households assigned to maintain the graves.

sentences.zh: 贈洵吏部尚書、汝南郡王，浩太常卿、武陵郡，洞衛尉卿、淮陽郡，泚太仆卿、上蔡郡，並葬京師。

translations.literal: Xun was posthumously given Minister of Personnel and Prince of Runan; Hao Grand Minister of Ceremonies and Prince of Wuling; Dong Commandant of the Court for the Imperial Clan and Prince of Huaiyang; Zhi Grand Master of the Imperial Stud and Prince of Shangcai—all buried in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was posthumously made Minister of Personnel and Prince of Runan; Hao Grand Minister of Ceremonies and Prince of Wuling; Dong Commandant of the Court for the Imperial Clan and Prince of Huaiyang; Zhi Grand Master of the Imperial Stud and Prince of Shangcai—all were buried in the capital.

sentences.zh: 溫初試吏，坐贓斥。

translations.literal: Wen first tried office but was dismissed for corruption.
translations.idiomatic: Wen first entered official service but was dismissed for corruption.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，擢宗正卿，遷禮部尚書，封魯國公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong he was promoted Director of the Imperial Clan and moved to Minister of Rites, enfeoffed Duke of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Shenlong he was promoted Director of the Imperial Clan, then Minister of Rites, and enfeoffed Duke of Lu.

sentences.zh: 弟湑，自洛州戶曹參軍事連拜左羽林大將軍，曹國公。

translations.literal: His younger brother Ji, from clerk in the Household Bureau of Luo Prefecture rose continuously to Grand General of the Left Feathered Forest and Duke of Cao.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Ji rose from a clerk in the Luo Prefecture revenue office to Grand General of the Left Feathered Forest and Duke of Cao.

sentences.zh: 后大妹嫁陸頌，進國子祭酒。

translations.literal: The empress's elder sister married Lu Song, who advanced to Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's elder sister married Lu Song, who rose to Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 仲妹嫁嗣虢王邕。

translations.literal: The second sister married the heir to Prince Guo of the second rank Yong.
translations.idiomatic: The second sister married Yong, heir to the second-rank Prince of Guo.

sentences.zh: 湑子捷尚成安公主，溫從弟濯尚定安公主，並拜駙馬都尉，捷為右羽林將軍。

translations.literal: Ji's son Jie married Princess Cheng'an; Wen's cousin Zhuan married Princess Ding'an—both were made Commandants of Cavalry; Jie became General of the Right Feathered Forest.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's son Jie married Princess Cheng'an; Wen's cousin Zhuan married Princess Ding'an. Both were made Commandants of Cavalry, and Jie became a general of the Right Feathered Forest.

sentences.zh: 景龍三年，溫以太子少保同中書門下三品，遙領揚州大都督。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jinglong, Wen was made Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince with concurrent status as Commissioner of the Secretariat and Chancellery, and remotely held Great Governor of Yang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jinglong, Wen was made Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince with concurrent status as Secretariat-Chancellery commissioner and titular Great Governor of Yang.

sentences.zh: 溫既見天下事在手，欲自殖以牢其權，引用友黨不相一，公卿雖畏伏，然溫無能，不如諸武兇而熾也。

translations.literal: Wen, seeing that the realm's affairs were in his hand, wished to enrich himself to secure his power; he drew in friends and partisans who were not of one mind; though the great ministers feared and submitted, Wen lacked ability and was not so fierce and blazing as the Wu clan.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the realm's affairs in his grasp, Wen wished to enrich himself to secure his power. He drew in friends and partisans who did not agree among themselves. Though the great ministers feared and submitted, Wen lacked ability and was not so fierce and overbearing as the Wu clan had been.

sentences.zh: 湑初兼脩文館大學士，時熒惑久留羽林，后惡之，方湑從至溫泉，后毒殺之以塞變，厚贈司徒、并州大都督。

translations.literal: Ji at first also held the post of Academician of the Xiuxian Hall; Mars had long remained in the Feathered Forest—a thing the empress hated; when Ji followed her to the hot springs she poisoned him to appease the omen, and lavishly posthumously gave him Minister of Works and Great Governor of Bing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ji had also served as an Academician of the Xiuxian Hall. Mars had long lingered in the Feathered Forest constellation, which the empress took as an ill omen. When Ji accompanied her to the hot springs she poisoned him to avert the sign and lavishly posthumously made him Minister of Works and Great Governor of Bing.

sentences.zh: 湑兄弟頗以文詞進，帝方盛選文章侍從，與賦詩相娛樂，湑雖為學士，常在北軍，無所造作。

translations.literal: The Ji brothers had risen somewhat on literary talent; the emperor was then lavishly selecting literary attendants for exchanging poems and amusement; though Ji was an academician he was always with the northern armies and produced nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The Ji brothers had risen partly on literary talent. The emperor was then lavishly selecting literary attendants for poetry and amusement. Though Ji was an academician he remained with the northern armies and wrote nothing of note.

sentences.zh: 有富商抵罪，萬年令李令質按之。

translations.literal: A wealthy merchant was charged with crime; the magistrate of Wannian Li Lingzhi investigated him.
translations.idiomatic: A wealthy merchant was charged with a crime, and the magistrate of Wannian, Li Lingzhi, investigated the case.

sentences.zh: 濯馳救，令質不從，毀於帝。

translations.literal: Zhuan hurried to rescue him; Lingzhi would not comply and reported him to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuan rushed to intervene, but Lingzhi refused and reported him to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝召令質至，左右為恐，令質從容曰：「濯於賊非親，但以貨為請，濯雖勢重，不如守陛下法，死無恨。」

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Lingzhi; attendants were afraid for him; Lingzhi said calmly: "Zhuan is not kin to the accused, but pleaded only for bribes; though Zhuan's power is great, it is not as good as upholding Your Majesty's laws—I die without regret.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Lingzhi. His attendants feared for him, but Lingzhi said calmly, "Zhuan is no kin to the accused—he pleaded only for a bribe. Though Zhuan's power is great, upholding Your Majesty's law is better. I die without regret.

sentences.zh: 帝釋不責。

translations.literal: The emperor released him without blame.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor released him without punishment.

sentences.zh: 帝崩，后專政，畏有變，敕溫盡總內外兵，守省中；

translations.literal: When the emperor died the empress monopolized government, fearing change; she ordered Wen to take complete charge of inner and outer troops and guard the palace precinct.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died the empress seized power, fearing a coup. She ordered Wen to command all inner and outer troops and guard the palace offices.

sentences.zh: 又以從子播、捷從弟璿、高嵩分領左右羽林軍。

translations.literal: She also had his nephew Bo and Jie, and cousins Xuan and Gao Song each command the left and right Feathered Forest armies.
translations.idiomatic: She also placed his nephews Bo and Jie and his cousins Xuan and Gao Song in command of the left and right Feathered Forest armies.

sentences.zh: 溫與宗楚客、武延秀等說后托圖讖，韋氏當受命，謀殺少帝，內憚相王、太平公主屬尊，欲先除之，然後發其謀。

translations.literal: Wen with Zong Chuke, Wu Yanxiu and others told the empress to rely on portents that the Wei clan was to receive the mandate; they plotted to kill the young emperor; inwardly they feared the Prince of Xiang and Princess Taiping were too honored and wished to remove them first, then carry out the plan.
translations.idiomatic: Wen joined Zong Chuke, Wu Yanxiu, and others in persuading the empress that portents showed the Wei clan was destined to rule. They plotted to kill the young emperor but feared the Prince of Xiang and Princess Taiping, who stood too high in honor, and wished to remove them first before carrying out the coup.

sentences.zh: 而玄宗兵夜起，將軍葛福順攻玄武門，入羽林，斬播、璿、高、嵩，梟首以徇，軍中相率而應，無敢後。

translations.literal: But Xuanzong's troops rose at night; General Ge Fushun attacked the Xuanwu Gate, entered the Feathered Forest, beheaded Bo, Xuan, Gao, and Song, displayed their heads as warning; the army one after another responded and none dared lag.
translations.idiomatic: But Xuanzong's troops rose by night. General Ge Fushun attacked the Xuanwu Gate, entered the Feathered Forest, and beheaded Bo, Xuan, Gao, and Song. Their heads were displayed as a warning, and the army followed one after another without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 后死，遲旦斬溫，分捕諸韋子弟，無少長皆斬。

translations.literal: The empress died; at dawn Wen was beheaded; they hunted down all Wei sons and nephews—young and old alike were executed.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was killed. At dawn Wen was beheaded. Wei sons and nephews were hunted down and executed without regard to age.

sentences.zh: 周仁軌

translations.literal: Zhou Rengui
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Rengui

sentences.zh: 周仁軌者，京兆萬年人，后母族也。

translations.literal: Zhou Rengui was a man of Wannian in Jingzhao, of the empress's mother's clan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Rengui was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao and belonged to the empress's mother's clan.

sentences.zh: 方為并州長史，殘酷嗜殺戮。

translations.literal: While serving as governor of Bing Prefecture he was cruel and addicted to killing.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as military governor of Bing he was cruel and addicted to slaughter.

sentences.zh: 異日，見堂下有斷臂，惡之，送於野，數昔往視，故在。

translations.literal: One day he saw a severed arm below the hall, detested it, and sent it to the wild; several evenings he went to look and it was still there.
translations.idiomatic: One day he saw a severed arm below the hall, was revolted, and had it cast into the wild. For several nights he went to look, and it was still there.

sentences.zh: 是月，韋后敗，使者誅仁軌，刑人舉刀，仁軌承以臂，墯地乃悟。

translations.literal: That month when Empress Wei fell, an envoy executed Rengui; as the executioner raised the blade Rengui presented his arm, fell to the ground, and then understood.
translations.idiomatic: That month, when Empress Wei fell, an envoy came to execute Rengui. As the headsman raised his blade Rengui held out his arm, fell to the ground, and only then understood the omen.

sentences.zh: 睿宗夷玄貞、洵墳墓，民盜取寶玉略盡。

translations.literal: Ruizong razed the tombs of Xuanzhen and Xun; the people stole jewels almost entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ruizong razed the tombs of Xuanzhen and Xun, and the people looted the jewels almost to the last piece.

sentences.zh: 天寶九載，復詔發掘，長安尉薛榮先往視，冢銘載葬日月，與發冢日月正同，而陵與尉名合雲。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Tianbao an edict again ordered exhumation; Chang'an magistrate Xue Rongxian went first to inspect; the tomb inscription recorded burial day and month identical to the day of exhumation, while the tomb and the magistrate's given name matched.
translations.idiomatic: In 750 an edict again ordered the tombs opened. Chang'an magistrate Xue Rongxian went to inspect them first. The tomb inscription recorded the burial date—the same day as the exhumation—and the tomb name and the magistrate's given name were taken as an omen.

sentences.zh: 王仁皎

translations.literal: Wang Renjiao
translations.idiomatic: Wang Renjiao

sentences.zh: 子守一，與后孿生，帝微時與雅舊，後詔尚清陽公主。

translations.literal: His son Shouyi was twin-born with the empress; when the emperor was in humble station they were old friends; later by edict he married Princess Qingyang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shouyi was the empress's twin. They had been friends when the emperor was still a private gentleman, and later an edict had Shouyi marry Princess Qingyang.

sentences.zh: 從討太平主有功，由尚乘奉御遷殿中少監、晉國公，累進太子少保，襲父爵，被遇良渥。

translations.literal: He shared in the campaign against Princess Taiping with merit; from Groom-in-Waiting of the Riding Office he was moved to Vice Director of the Palace Domestic Service and Duke of Jin, rose repeatedly to Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince, inherited his father's title, and was favored richly.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the campaign against Princess Taiping and was rewarded. From groom of the imperial stables he rose to Vice Director of the Palace Service and Duke of Jin, then to Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince. He inherited his father's title and enjoyed exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 后廢，貶柳州別駕，至藍田，賜死。

translations.literal: When the empress was deposed he was demoted Vice Prefect of Liuzhou; at Lantian he was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress was deposed he was demoted to vice prefect of Liuzhou. At Lantian he was granted death.

sentences.zh: 守一沓墨無顧藉，財蓄巨萬，皆籍入於官。

translations.literal: Shouyi was reckless with ink and without restraint; treasure in the millions—all was registered into the state treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyi was corrupt and unrestrained. His wealth ran to millions, and all of it was confiscated for the state.

sentences.zh: 楊國忠

translations.literal: Yang Guozhong
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong

sentences.zh: 楊國忠，太真妃之從祖兄，張易之之出也。

translations.literal: Yang Guozhong was the elder cousin in the senior line of Consort Taizhen, offspring of Zhang Yizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong was a senior cousin of Consort Taizhen and a son of Zhang Yizhi's house.

sentences.zh: 嗜飲博，數丐貸於人，無行檢，不為姻族齒。

translations.literal: He was addicted to drink and gambling, often begged loans from others, without propriety—not ranked among affinal kin.
translations.idiomatic: He was addicted to drink and gambling, constantly borrowing from others, without propriety. His kin by marriage would not acknowledge him.

sentences.zh: 年三十從蜀軍，以屯優當遷，節度使張宥惡其人，笞屈之，然卒以優為新都尉。

translations.literal: At thirty he joined the Shu army; because of camp entertainment he was to be promoted, but Military Commissioner Zhang You hated him, flogged and humiliated him, yet in the end he became magistrate of Xindu on account of his entertainment skill.
translations.idiomatic: At thirty he joined the Shu army. His skill as a camp entertainer was grounds for promotion, but Military Commissioner Zhang You detested him, flogged and humiliated him, yet in the end made him magistrate of Xindu for his performances.

sentences.zh: 罷去，益困，蜀大豪鮮于仲通頗資給之。

translations.literal: When he left office he grew poorer; the great magnate of Shu Xianyu Zhongtong often subsidized him.
translations.idiomatic: When he left office he grew still poorer. The great Shu magnate Xianyu Zhongtong often supported him.

sentences.zh: 從父玄琰死蜀州，國忠護視其家，因與妹通，所謂虢國夫人者。

translations.literal: When his father's younger brother Xuanyan died in Shu Prefecture, Guozhong guarded and watched the household and thereby had relations with his sister—the one called the Lady of Guo.
translations.idiomatic: When his uncle Xuanyan died in Shu, Guozhong looked after the household and took his sister as a lover—the woman later known as the Lady of Guo.

sentences.zh: 裒其貲，至成都摴蒲，一日費輒盡，乃亡去。

translations.literal: He gathered her goods; reaching Chengdu he gambled, spending it all in a day, then fled.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered her property, went to Chengdu to gamble, spent it all in a single day, and fled.

sentences.zh: 久之，調扶風尉，不得誌。

translations.literal: After long time he was transferred magistrate of Fufeng but could not achieve his ambition.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was transferred to magistrate of Fufeng but could not fulfill his ambitions.

sentences.zh: 復入蜀，劍南節度使章仇兼瓊與宰相李林甫不平，聞楊氏新有寵，思有以結納之為奧助，使仲通之長安，仲通辭，以國忠見，幹貌頎峻，口辯給，兼瓊喜，表為推官，使部春貢長安。

translations.literal: Again he entered Shu; Military Commissioner of Jiannan Zhang Qiu Jianqiong was at odds with Chancellor Li Linpu; hearing the Yang clan had new favor he thought to win them as inside help; he had Zhongtong go to Chang'an—Zhongtong declined, but showed Guozhong; lean and tall of bearing, glib in speech—Jianqiong was pleased, memorialized him as pushing officer, sent him to lead the spring tribute to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to Shu. Jiannan Military Commissioner Zhang Qiu Jianqiong was at odds with Chancellor Li Linpu. Hearing that the Yang clan had newly risen in favor, he sought a connection as an inside ally. He sent Zhongtong to Chang'an; Zhongtong declined but presented Guozhong—lean, tall, and quick of tongue. Jianqiong was pleased, recommended him as a staff officer, and sent him to lead the spring tribute mission to the capital.

sentences.zh: 將行，告曰：「郫有一日糧，君至，可取之也。」

translations.literal: On departing he said: "At Pi there is one day's provisions—when you arrive you may take them.
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to leave, Jianqiong told him, "At Pi you will find a day's provisions—take them when you arrive.

sentences.zh: 國忠至，乃得蜀貨百萬，即大喜。

translations.literal: Guozhong arrived and obtained Shu goods worth a million—then was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong arrived and found Shu goods worth a million. He was overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 至京師，見群女弟，致贈遺。

translations.literal: Reaching the capital he saw the cluster of younger sisters and sent them gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital he visited his younger sisters and sent them gifts.

sentences.zh: 於時虢國新寡，國忠多分賂，宣淫不止。

translations.literal: At that time the Lady of Guo was newly widowed; Guozhong divided much of the bribes and carried on lewdness without cease.
translations.idiomatic: The Lady of Guo was then newly widowed. Guozhong gave her a large share of the gifts and carried on an open affair with her without cease.

sentences.zh: 諸楊日為兼瓊譽，而言國忠善摴蒲，玄宗引見，擢金吾兵曹參軍、閑廄判官。

translations.literal: The Yangs daily praised Jianqiong and said Guozhong was skilled at gambling; Xuanzong summoned and met him, promoted him Gentleman of Cavalry in the Golden Guard and Adjutant of the Imperial Stables.
translations.idiomatic: The Yangs daily praised Jianqiong and said Guozhong was skilled at dice. Xuanzong summoned him, made him a cavalry officer in the Golden Guard, and appointed him adjutant of the imperial stables.

sentences.zh: 兼瓊入為戶部尚書兼御史大夫，用其力也。

translations.literal: Jianqiong entered as Minister of Revenue and concurrent Censor-in-Chief—through Guozhong's power.
translations.idiomatic: Jianqiong entered court as Minister of Revenue and concurrent Censor-in-Chief through Guozhong's influence.

sentences.zh: 國忠稍入供奉，常後出，專主薄簿，計算鉤畫，分銖不誤，帝悅曰：「度支郎才也。」

translations.literal: Guozhong gradually entered attendance duties, often lingering late, exclusively managing thin ledgers; calculating and hooking accounts, not missing a fen—the emperor was pleased and said: "A Revenue Section officer's talent.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong gradually joined the emperor's attendance staff, often staying late to manage the ledgers himself. His calculations were exact to the last cash. The emperor was pleased and said, "Here is a revenue officer's talent.

sentences.zh: 累遷監察御史。

translations.literal: He rose repeatedly to Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 李林甫興韋堅等獄，欲危太子，獄事畏卻，以國忠怙寵，搏鷙可用，倚之使按劾。

translations.literal: Li Linpu engineered the cases of Wei Jian and others, wishing to endanger the crown prince; the cases feared setback—for Guozhong relied on favor and was fierce and usable—he leaned on him to conduct investigations.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linpu engineered the cases of Wei Jian and others to endanger the crown prince. When the prosecutions stalled, he turned to Guozhong, who enjoyed imperial favor and was fierce and pliable, and relied on him to conduct the investigations.

sentences.zh: 國忠乃慘文峭詆，逮系連年，誣蔑被誅者百餘族，度可以危太子者，先林甫意陷之，皆中所欲。

translations.literal: Guozhong then wrote cruel, twisting indictments; year after year arrests and links; slander caused execution of more than a hundred clans; whoever could endanger the crown prince he first according to Linpu's intent entrapped—all hit what was desired.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong drafted cruel, twisting indictments. Year after year arrests multiplied, and slander sent more than a hundred clans to execution. Whoever might threaten the crown prince he entrapped ahead of Linpu's intent—all to Linpu's satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 林甫方深阻固位，陰為指向，故國忠乘以為奸，肆意無所憚。

translations.literal: Linpu was at the time deeply obstructing to secure position and secretly pointed the direction; therefore Guozhong took this to do evil and acted without fear.
translations.idiomatic: Linpu was then deeply entrenched and secretly steered the prosecutions, so Guozhong used the opening to do evil and acted without fear.

sentences.zh: 虢國居中用事，帝所好惡，國忠必探知其微，帝以為能，擢兼度支員外郎。

translations.literal: The Lady of Guo held sway at center; whatever the emperor liked or hated Guozhong was sure to probe the subtle points—the emperor thought him capable and promoted him concurrent Vice Director of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: The Lady of Guo held sway at court. Whatever the emperor favored or disliked, Guozhong probed the subtle signs. The emperor thought him capable and made him concurrent Vice Director of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 遷不淹年，領十五餘使，林甫始惡之。

translations.literal: Within less than a year he held more than fifteen commissions; Linpu began to hate him.
translations.idiomatic: Within less than a year he held more than fifteen commissions, and Linpu began to hate him.

sentences.zh: 天寶七載，擢給事中、兼御史中丞，專判度支。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tianbao he was promoted Draftsman and concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief, exclusively judging revenue affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 748 he was promoted to Draftsman and concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief, with exclusive charge of revenue affairs.

sentences.zh: 會三妹封國夫人，兄铦擢鴻臚卿，與國忠皆列棨戟，而第舍華僭，彌跨都邑。

translations.literal: When the three younger sisters were enfeoffed ladies of state, elder brother Xian was promoted Chamberlain for Ceremonials—in company with Guozhong all bore ceremonial lances, while residences were lavish beyond measure, dominating the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When his three younger sisters were enfeoffed as ladies of state, his elder brother Xian was made Chamberlain for Ceremonials. He and Guozhong both bore ceremonial lances, and their mansions grew so lavish they dominated the capital.

sentences.zh: 時海內豐熾，州縣粟帛舉巨萬，國忠因言：古者二十七年耕，餘九年食，今天置太平，請在所出滯積，變輕賫，內富京師。

translations.literal: At the time within the seas were abundant; counties and prefectures reported grain and silk by the tens of millions; Guozhong thereupon said: In antiquity twenty-seven years of farming left nine years of eating; today peace is established—he requested wherever surplus piled up to convert to light goods and enrich the capital within.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was then abundantly prosperous; counties and prefectures reported grain and silk in the tens of millions. Guozhong argued that in antiquity twenty-seven years of farming supplied nine years of eating, whereas now peace reigned. He asked that local surpluses be converted to portable goods to enrich the capital.

sentences.zh: 又悉天下義倉及丁租、地課易布帛，以充天子禁藏。

translations.literal: Again he exchanged all the realm's charity granaries with corvée and land taxes for cloth and silk to fill the Son of Heaven's forbidden storehouses.
translations.idiomatic: He also converted the empire's charity granaries and corvée and land taxes into cloth and silk to fill the emperor's private treasuries.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝詔百官觀庫物，積如丘山，賜群臣各有差，錫國忠紫衣、金魚，知太府卿事。

translations.literal: The next year the emperor ordered the hundred officials to view storehouse goods piled like hills and mountains; he bestowed gifts on the ministers each by rank, conferred on Guozhong purple robes and golden fish, and made him overseer of Grand Storehouse affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the emperor had the officials view the treasury stores, heaped like hills. He bestowed gifts on the ministers by rank, granted Guozhong purple robes and the golden fish insignia, and put him in charge of the Grand Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 初，楊慎矜引王鉷為御史中丞，已而有隙。

translations.literal: At first Yang Shenjin introduced Wang Qiu as Vice Censor-in-Chief; afterward they had a rift.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yang Shenjin had recommended Wang Qiu as Vice Censor-in-Chief, but they later fell out.

sentences.zh: 鉷挾國忠共劾慎矜，抵不道，誅。

translations.literal: Qiu together with Guozhong impeached Shenjin; he was charged with impiety and executed.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu joined Guozhong in impeaching Shenjin. He was charged with impiety and executed.

sentences.zh: 由是權傾中外。

translations.literal: Thereby power tilted inside and outside.
translations.idiomatic: From then on his power dominated court and realm.

sentences.zh: 吉溫為國忠謀奪林甫政，國忠即誣奏京兆尹蕭炅、御史中丞宋渾，逐之，皆林甫所厚善，林甫不能救，遂結怨。

translations.literal: Ji Wen plotted for Guozhong to seize Linpu's government; Guozhong at once fabricated memorials against Yongzhou Magistrate Xiao Jiong and Vice Censor-in-Chief Song Hun, drove them out—both were those Linpu favored; Linpu could not save them and thus bore a grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Wen plotted with Guozhong to seize power from Linpu. Guozhong at once fabricated charges against Yongzhou Magistrate Xiao Jiong and Vice Censor-in-Chief Song Hun and had them driven out. Both were Linpu's favorites, and Linpu could not save them. A grudge was born.

sentences.zh: 鉷寵方渥，位勢在國忠右，國忠忌之，因邢縡事，構鉷誅死，己代為京兆尹，悉領其使。

translations.literal: Qiu's favor was then thick, rank and power above Guozhong; Guozhong envied him and through the Xing Zan affair framed Qiu to execution and death; he himself replaced Qiu as Yongzhou Magistrate and took all his commissions.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu's favor was then at its height and his rank above Guozhong's. Guozhong envied him and, through the Xing Zan affair, framed him to execution. Guozhong replaced him as Yongzhou magistrate and took over all his commissions.

sentences.zh: 即窮劾支黨，引林甫交私狀，牽連左逮，數以聞，帝始厭林甫，疏薄之。

translations.literal: He then pursued impeachment to the extremity of affiliated parties, drawing out Linpu's private dealings with associates, implicating and arresting on the left, reporting repeatedly to the emperor—the emperor began to weary of Linpu and grew distant and thin in favor.
translations.idiomatic: He then pursued the affiliated parties to the end, exposing Linpu's private dealings and implicating his associates in arrests. Report after report reached the emperor, who began to weary of Linpu and grew distant from him.

sentences.zh: 先此，南詔質子閤羅鳳亡去，帝欲討之，國忠薦鮮于仲通為蜀郡長史，率兵六萬討之。

translations.literal: Before this, the Nanzhao hostage Piluoge had fled; the emperor wished to campaign; Guozhong recommended Xianyu Zhongtong as governor of Shu and Leader of sixty thousand troops to campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Nanzhao hostage Piluoge had fled. The emperor wished to punish Nanzhao, and Guozhong recommended Xianyu Zhongtong as Shu commandery governor to lead sixty thousand men against them.

sentences.zh: 戰瀘川，舉軍沒，獨仲通挺身免。

translations.literal: They fought at Luzhou; the whole army was lost; only Zhongtong alone escaped by presenting his body.
translations.idiomatic: They fought at Luzhou. The entire army was destroyed; only Zhongtong escaped alive.

sentences.zh: 時國忠兼兵部侍郎，素德仲通，為匿其敗，更敘戰功，使白衣領職。

translations.literal: At the time Guozhong was also Vice Minister of War and had long been obliged to Zhongtong; he concealed the defeat, rearranged battle merit, and had him lead office while still in plain dress.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong was then also Vice Minister of War and owed Zhongtong a debt of gratitude. He concealed the defeat, fabricated a record of merit, and let Zhongtong hold office while still in plain clothes.

sentences.zh: 因自請兼領劍南，詔拜劍南節度、支度、營田副大使，知節度事。

translations.literal: He then requested himself to take concurrent charge of Jiannan; an edict appointed him Deputy Military Commissioner of Jiannan for expenditure, farming, and headquarters, with knowledge of military commission affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked to take concurrent command of Jiannan and was appointed deputy military commissioner of Jiannan for expenditure, farming, and headquarters, with full authority over the circuit.

sentences.zh: 俄加本道兼山南西道采訪處置使，開幕府，引竇華、張漸、宋昱、鄭昂、魏仲犀等自佐，而留京師。

translations.literal: Soon he added commissary for his circuit and concurrently for the Shannan West circuit; he opened a headquarters and recruited Dou Hua, Zhang Jian, Song Yu, Zheng Ang, Wei Zhongxi and others as aides, while remaining in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was also made commissary for Jiannan and concurrently for Shannan West. He opened a staff office and recruited Dou Hua, Zhang Jian, Song Yu, Zheng Ang, Wei Zhongxi, and others as aides, while he himself remained in the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝再幸左藏庫，班賫百官。

translations.literal: The emperor again visited the Left Storehouse and distributed gifts to the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again visited the Left Treasury and distributed gifts among the officials.

sentences.zh: 出納判官魏仲犀言：「鳳集通訓門。」

translations.literal: Disbursement judging officer Wei Zhongxi said: "A phoenix gathered at the Tongxun Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Disbursement officer Wei Zhongxi reported, "A phoenix has gathered at the Tongxun Gate.

sentences.zh: 門直庫西，有詔改為鳳皇門，進仲犀殿中侍御史，屬吏率以「鳳凰優」得調。

translations.literal: The gate faced west of the storehouse; by edict it was renamed Phoenix Gate; Zhongxi was promoted Palace Attendant Censor; subordinate officials mostly gained transfer through the "phoenix omen."
translations.idiomatic: The gate faced the treasury's west side. An edict renamed it Phoenix Gate. Zhongxi was promoted to Palace Attendant Censor, and subordinates mostly won transfers by invoking the "phoenix omen."

sentences.zh: 俄拜國忠御史大夫，因引仲通為京兆尹，己兼領吏部。

translations.literal: Soon Guozhong was made Censor-in-Chief; thereby Zhongtong was introduced as Yongzhou Magistrate, while he himself also held concurrent charge of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Guozhong was made Censor-in-Chief. He installed Zhongtong as Yongzhou magistrate while he himself also held the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 國忠恥雲南無功，知為林甫掎摭，欲自解於帝，乃使麾下請己到屯，外示憂邊，以合上旨，實杜禁言路，林甫果奏遣之。

translations.literal: Guozhong was ashamed of Yunnan's no merit, knew Linpu had seized and exposed him, wished to clear himself with the emperor—therefore he had his subordinates request that he come to the garrison, outwardly showing concern for the border to match the emperor's intent, while in fact blocking the path of remonstrance; Linpu indeed memorialized to send him.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong was ashamed of the failed Yunnan campaign and knew Linpu had seized on the matter to attack him. Wishing to clear himself with the emperor, he had his followers petition that he be sent to the frontier garrison, outwardly showing concern for the border to match the emperor's wishes while in fact silencing criticism. Linpu duly memorialized to send him.

sentences.zh: 及辭，泣訴為林甫中傷者，妃又為言，故帝益親之，豫計召日。

translations.literal: When taking leave he wept and complained that Linpu had slandered and injured him; the consort spoke for him again, so the emperor drew closer to him and calculated in advance the day of recall.
translations.idiomatic: At his farewell he wept and pleaded that Li Linpu had slandered him; Yang Guifei spoke for him again, and the emperor grew still fonder of him, counting the days until he could summon him back.

sentences.zh: 然國忠就道，惴惴不自安。

translations.literal: Yet as Guozhong took the road he was fearful and ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Yet as Yang Guozhong set out on the road, dread gnawed at him and he could find no peace.

sentences.zh: 帝在華清宮，驛追國忠還。

translations.literal: The emperor was at Huaqing Palace and sent post-horses to recall Guozhong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was at Huaqing Palace and sent couriers by post to bring Guozhong back.

sentences.zh: 林甫病已困，入見床下，林甫曰：「死矣，公且入相，以後事屬公！」

translations.literal: Linpu's illness was already dire; entering he saw him beside the bed. Linpu said: "I am dying. You will soon enter the chancellery—the affairs hereafter I entrust to you!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Linpu was already gravely ill. Guozhong went in and found him by the bedside. Linpu said, "I am dying. You will soon be chancellor—entrust what comes after to you!"

sentences.zh: 國忠懼其詐，不敢當，流汗被顏。

translations.literal: Guozhong feared it was a trick and dared not accept; sweat drenched his face.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong feared a trap and dared not accept; sweat streamed down his face.

sentences.zh: 林甫果死，遂拜右相，兼文部尚書、集賢院大學士、監脩國史、崇賢館大學士、太清太微宮使，而節度、采訪等使、判度支，不解也。

translations.literal: Linpu indeed died; he was then appointed Right Chancellor, concurrently Minister of Rites, Academician of the Jixian Institute, Supervisor of Compiling the National History, Academician of the Chongxian Hall, Commissioner of the Taqing and Taiwei Palaces, while his posts as military commissioner, recruitment commissioner, and controller of the Board of Revenue were not relinquished.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linpu did die. Guozhong was then made Right Chancellor, with concurrent posts as Minister of Rites, Jixian Academician, Supervisor of the National History, Chongxian Academician, and Commissioner of the Taqing and Taiwei Palaces—while he kept his military commissions, recruitment duties, and control of the Board of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 國忠已得柄，則窮擿林甫奸事，碎其家。

translations.literal: Once Guozhong had grasped power he thoroughly exposed Linpu's corrupt deeds and shattered his household.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held real power, Guozhong dug up every charge against Li Linpu and ruined his house.

sentences.zh: 帝以為功，封魏國公，固讓魏，徙封衛。

translations.literal: The emperor regarded it as merit and enfeoffed him Duke of Wei; he firmly declined Wei and was transferred to Duke of Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took this for merit and enfeoffed him Duke of Wei; he firmly declined the character Wei and was made Duke of Guard instead.

sentences.zh: 國忠既以宰相領選，始建罷長名，於銓日即定留放。

translations.literal: Guozhong having taken charge of selections as chancellor, first instituted abolishing the long roster; on the day of evaluation retainees and dismissals were fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Now that he was chancellor and oversaw appointments, Guozhong first abolished the long waiting list and fixed who would stay or go on the very day of evaluation.

sentences.zh: 故事，歲揭版南院為選式，選者自通，一辭不如式，輒不得調，故有十年不官者。

translations.literal: By precedent each year boards were posted in the southern courtyard as the selection form; candidates reported themselves, and if one presentation did not meet the form they could not be assigned—there were some who went ten years without office.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, each year the selection rules were posted in the southern courtyard; candidates presented themselves, and if a single submission failed the format they could not be assigned—some men went ten years without an office.

sentences.zh: 國忠創押例，無賢不肖，用選深者先補官，牒文謬缺得再通，眾議翕然美之。

translations.literal: Guozhong created the sealed-warrant precedent: whether worthy or unworthy, those with deep selection seniority were first given office; if the document had errors or gaps they could report again; public opinion united in praising it.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong introduced an expedited rule: worthy or not, those with the longest waiting time were appointed first; flawed documents could be resubmitted—and opinion united in praise.

sentences.zh: 先天以前，諸司官知政事者，午漏盡，還本司視事，兵、吏部尚書、侍郎分案註擬。

translations.literal: Before the Xiantian era, officials in various bureaus who attended to state affairs, when the midday clepsydra ran out, returned to their home bureaus to handle business; the Ministers and Vice Ministers of War and Personnel divided cases and drafted nominations.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Xiantian era, officials who handled state affairs in the various ministries, once the midday water-clock ran out, returned to their own offices to conduct business; the Ministers and Vice Ministers of War and Personnel divided the cases and drafted nominations.

sentences.zh: 開元末，宰相員少，任益尊，不復視本司事。

translations.literal: At the end of the Kaiyuan era the number of chancellors was few, their responsibility grew more exalted, and they no longer attended to their home bureau affairs.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of Kaiyuan there were few chancellors, their standing had grown more exalted, and they no longer handled their home ministries' affairs.

sentences.zh: 吏部銓，故常三註三唱，自春止夏乃訖。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel's evaluation, by custom, had three rounds of nomination and three announcements, from spring until summer before finishing.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel's evaluation, by custom, ran three rounds of nomination and three announcements, from spring through summer before it ended.

sentences.zh: 而國忠陰使吏到第，預定其員，集百官尚書省註唱，一日畢，以誇神明，駭天下耳目者。

translations.literal: But Guozhong secretly had clerks come to his residence, predetermining the quotas; he gathered all officials at the Ministry of Personnel for nomination and announcement, finishing in one day—to boast divine speed and startle the empire's ears and eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong, however, secretly had clerks come to his house to fix the quotas in advance, then gathered the officials at the Ministry for nomination and announcement in a single day—to boast supernatural speed and startle the empire.

sentences.zh: 自是資格紛謬，無復綱序。

translations.literal: From this qualifications were confused and mistaken; there was no restoration of orderly sequence.
translations.idiomatic: From then on qualifications were a tangle of errors, and orderly precedence was gone.

sentences.zh: 虢國居宣陽坊左，國忠在其南，自臺禁還，趣虢國第，郎官、御史白事者皆隨以至。

translations.literal: Guoguo lived at the left of Xuanyang Ward; Guozhong was south of her; returning from the Censorate and palace gates he would hasten to Guoguo's residence, and examining censors and attendants reporting business all followed him there.
translations.idiomatic: Guoguo lived on the left side of Xuanyang Ward; Guozhong's house lay to her south. Returning from the Censorate and the palace gates he would hurry to Guoguo's mansion, and examining censors and attendants with business all trailed after him.

sentences.zh: 居同第，出駢騎，相調笑，施施若禽獸然，不以為羞，道路為恥駭。

translations.literal: They lived in the same compound, went out in paired horses, bantered and teased—proceeding leisurely like birds and beasts, not taking it as shame; the roads were shamed and horrified.
translations.idiomatic: They shared one compound, rode out in matched teams of horses, bantering and laughing as they strolled along like birds and beasts, unashamed—while passersby were appalled.

sentences.zh: 明年大選，因就第唱補，帷女兄弟觀之，士之鬼野蹇傴者，呼其名，輒笑於堂，聲徹諸外，士大夫詬恥之。

translations.literal: The next year at the great selection he conducted nomination appointments at his residence; behind a curtain his sisters watched. Candidates who were gaunt rustic stooping fellows—calling their names they would laugh in the hall, the sound penetrating outside; scholar-officials reviled and shamed it.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, at the great selection, he held the appointment ceremony at his own house while his sisters watched from behind a curtain. When emaciated, bent country candidates were called by name, the women burst out laughing in the hall until the sound carried outside—scholar-officials were disgusted and ashamed.

sentences.zh: 先是，有司已定註，則過門下，侍中、給事中按閱，有不可，黜之。

translations.literal: Previously when the authorities had fixed nominations they passed through the Gate Department; the attendant grandee and reviewer examined, and if something was unacceptable they dismissed it.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, once nominations were set, they went through the Gate Department, where the attendant grandee and the reviewing drafter examined them and struck down what was unfit.

sentences.zh: 國忠則召左相陳希烈隅坐，給事中在旁，既對註，曰：「已過門下矣。」

translations.literal: Guozhong instead summoned Left Chancellor Chen Xilie to sit in a corner, the reviewer at his side; after the nominations were matched he said: "Already passed the Gate Department.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong instead called Left Chancellor Chen Xilie to sit in a corner with the reviewing drafter beside him; when nominations were read out he would say, "Already passed the Gate Department.

sentences.zh: 希烈不敢異。

translations.literal: Xilie dared not disagree.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie dared not object.

sentences.zh: 侍郎韋見素、張倚與本曹郎趨走堂下，抱案牒，國忠顧女弟曰：「紫袍二主事何如？」

translations.literal: Vice Ministers Wei Jiansu and Zhang Yi with the bureau clerks hurried below the hall carrying case documents; Guozhong turned to his sister and said: "How about two directors in purple robes?
translations.idiomatic: Vice Ministers Wei Jiansu and Zhang Yi hurried below the hall with their clerks clutching the registers; Guozhong glanced at his sister and said, "What do you think of two purple-robed bureau directors?

sentences.zh: 皆大噱。

translations.literal: All roared with laughter.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone roared with laughter.

sentences.zh: 鮮于仲通等諷選者鄭怤願立碑省戶下以頌德，詔仲通為頌，帝為易數字，因以黃金識其處。

translations.literal: Xianyu Zhongtong and others hinted to the candidate Zheng Wu that he wished to erect a stele beneath the ministry gate to praise his virtue; the edict had Zhongtong compose the encomium, the emperor altered several characters, and thereby marked the place in gold.
translations.idiomatic: Xianyu Zhongtong and others prompted the candidate Zheng Wu to propose erecting a stele under the ministry gate to praise Guozhong's virtue. The emperor had Zhongtong write the inscription, changed several characters himself, and marked those spots in gold.

sentences.zh: 帝常歲十月幸華清宮，春乃還，而諸楊湯沐館在宮東垣，連蔓相照，帝臨幸，必遍五家，賞賫不訾計，出有賜，曰「餞路」，返有勞，曰「軟腳」。

translations.literal: The emperor commonly in the tenth month visited Huaqing Palace and returned in spring; the various Yang bathing lodges were on the palace's eastern wall, their vines shining on one another; when the emperor visited he necessarily went to all five households; rewards beyond reckoning; going out there were gifts called "farewell road"; returning there was thanks called "soft foot."
translations.idiomatic: Each year in the tenth month the emperor would visit Huaqing Palace and return in spring. The Yang clan's bathhouses lined the eastern wall of the palace, their vines interlaced in light. Whenever the emperor came he visited all five households in turn, lavishing gifts beyond counting. Departing, he gave "road-fare" rewards; on return, "soft-foot" thanks.

sentences.zh: 遠近饋遺閹稚、歌兒、狗馬、金貝，踵疊其門。

translations.literal: From near and far came gifts—eunuch boys, singing girls, dogs, horses, gold and shells—piling at their gates in layers.
translations.idiomatic: From near and far came gifts—eunuch boys, singing girls, dogs, horses, gold and treasure—heaped layer upon layer at their gates.

sentences.zh: 國忠由御史至宰相，凡領四十餘使，而度支、吏部事自叢夥，第署一字不能盡，故吏得輕重，顯賕公謁無所忌。

translations.literal: From censor to chancellor Guozhong in total held more than forty commissions; yet the Board of Revenue and Ministry of Personnel affairs were especially numerous, so that at his residence he could not finish signing a single character, and thus clerks could weight light and heavy; open bribery and audience had no fear.
translations.idiomatic: From censor to chancellor Guozhong held more than forty commissions in all. Revenue and personnel matters alone were so vast that he could not finish signing a single character at home, so clerks could tip the scales—and open bribery at his door knew no restraint.

sentences.zh: 國忠性疏侻捷給，硁硁處決樞務，自任不疑，盛氣驕愎，百僚莫敢相可否，官屬悉苛督句剝相槊。

translations.literal: Guozhong's nature was careless and sharp-tongued, quick in deciding pivot affairs, trusting himself without doubt, overbearing and proud—no hundred officials dared dispute yes or no; his subordinates all rigorously supervised collection and mutual squeezing.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong was careless yet glib, quick to decide affairs at the pivot of power, trusting himself utterly, overbearing and proud—no official dared contradict him, and his staff drove collection and squeezing to extremes.

sentences.zh: 又便佞，專徇帝嗜欲，不顧天下成敗。

translations.literal: He was also fawning, exclusively following the emperor's appetites without regard for the empire's success or failure.
translations.idiomatic: He was sycophantic as well, indulging the emperor's every whim without regard for whether the realm prospered or fell.

sentences.zh: 帝雅意事邊，故身調兵食，取習文簿惡吏任之，軍凡須索，快成其手，又不能省視也。

translations.literal: The emperor by temperament favored frontier affairs; hence he personally adjusted troops and grain, took clerks skilled in paperwork but of bad character and employed them; whatever the army required was quickly produced at his hand, yet he could not economize and inspect either.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor by nature cared for frontier affairs, so Guozhong personally handled troops and supplies, appointing clerks who were skilled with documents but corrupt; whatever the armies needed he produced at once, yet he never audited the cost.

sentences.zh: 始，李林甫紿帝天下無事，請巳漏出休，許之。

translations.literal: At first Li Linpu deceived the emperor that under heaven there were no troubles, and requested that after the ninth hour he leave to rest; it was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: At first Li Linpu had deceived the emperor into believing the realm was at peace and asked leave to rest after the ninth hour of the day; permission was granted.

sentences.zh: 文書填湊，坐家裁決。

translations.literal: Documents piled up; seated at home he decided them.
translations.idiomatic: Documents piled up, and he decided them seated at home.

sentences.zh: 既成，敕吏持案詣左相陳希烈聯署，左相不敢詰，署惟謹。

translations.literal: When finished he ordered clerks to bring the drafts to Left Chancellor Chen Xilie for joint signature; the left chancellor dared not question and signed with utmost care.
translations.idiomatic: When done, he had clerks carry the drafts to Left Chancellor Chen Xilie for joint signature; the left chancellor dared not question anything and signed with meticulous care.

sentences.zh: 至國忠時，韋見素代希烈，循以為常。

translations.literal: By Guozhong's time Wei Jiansu replaced Xilie and followed it as routine.
translations.idiomatic: In Guozhong's day Wei Jiansu replaced Xilie and the practice continued unchanged.

sentences.zh: 它年，大雨敗稼，帝憂之，國忠擇善禾以進，曰：「雨不為災。」

translations.literal: Another year great rain ruined the crops; the emperor was troubled; Guozhong selected good grain stalks to present and said: "The rain has not made a disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Another year heavy rains ruined the harvest and the emperor was troubled. Guozhong picked healthy stalks to present and said, "The rain has done no harm.

sentences.zh: 扶風太守房琯上郡災，國忠怒，遣御史按之。

translations.literal: Fufeng Prefect Fang Guan reported the commandery disaster; Guozhong was enraged and sent an examining censor to investigate him.
translations.idiomatic: Fufeng prefect Fang Guan reported the disaster in his commandery; Guozhong was furious and sent a censor to investigate him.

sentences.zh: 後乃無敢以水旱聞，皆前伺國忠意乃敢啟。

translations.literal: Afterward none dared report flood or drought; all first watched Guozhong's intent before daring to open memorials.
translations.idiomatic: After that no one dared report flood or drought until they had first gauged Guozhong's mood.

sentences.zh: 子暄舉明經，不中，禮部侍郎達奚珣遣子撫往見國忠，國忠方朝，見撫喜。

translations.literal: His son Xuan passed the Mingjing examination but failed; Vice Minister of Rites Daxi Xun sent his son Fu to see Guozhong; Guozhong was just at court and seeing Fu was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xuan took the Mingjing examination and failed. Vice Minister of Rites Daxi Xun sent his son Fu to call on Guozhong, who was at court and delighted to see him.

sentences.zh: 已而聞暄當黜，詬曰：「生子不富貴耶？

translations.literal: Shortly he heard Xuan was to be dismissed and cursed: "Bear a son yet not wealthy and noble?
translations.idiomatic: Soon he learned Xuan was to be failed and cursed, "You have a son and he is not rich and noble?

sentences.zh: 豈以一名為鼠輩所賣！」

translations.literal: Can one office be sold to scum like rats!
translations.idiomatic: Would you let some rat sell you a single rank!

sentences.zh: 珣大驚，即致暄高第。

translations.literal: Xun was greatly alarmed and immediately gave Xuan top rank.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was terrified and at once placed Xuan at the top of the list.

sentences.zh: 俄與珣同列，猶咤官不進。

translations.literal: Soon he was the same rank as Xun, yet still gasped that office did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he stood at the same rank as Xun, yet still complained that his office had not risen higher.

sentences.zh: 國忠雖當國，常領劍南召募使，遣戍瀘南，餉路險乏，舉無還者。

translations.literal: Though Guozhong controlled the state he constantly held the Jiannan recruitment commission, sent garrisons to southern Lu, the supply route perilous and deficient—not one returned.
translations.idiomatic: Though Guozhong ruled the state he still kept the Jiannan recruitment commission, sending men to garrison southern Lu; the supply route was deadly and bare—not one came back.

sentences.zh: 舊，勛戶免行，所以寵戰功。

translations.literal: By precedent meritorious households were exempt from service, to honor battle achievement.
translations.idiomatic: By custom households with battle honors were exempt from the draft, a reward for military merit.

sentences.zh: 國忠令當行者先取勛家，故士無鬥誌。

translations.literal: Guozhong ordered that those due to go first take merit households, so warriors had no fighting will.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong ordered that draftees be taken first from merit households, so soldiers lost all will to fight.

sentences.zh: 凡募法，願奮者則籍之。

translations.literal: Generally in the recruitment law, those willing to strive were registered.
translations.idiomatic: Under the recruitment law, men who volunteered were supposed to be registered.

sentences.zh: 國忠歲遣宋昱、鄭昂、韋儇以御史迫促，郡縣吏窮無以應，乃詭設餉召貧弱者，密縛置室中，衣絮衣，械而送屯，亡者以送吏代之，人人思亂。

translations.literal: Each year Guozhong sent Song Yu, Zheng Ang, and Wei Yan as censors to press urgently; commandery and district clerks were exhausted with nothing to respond and so falsely set up supply recruitment calling the poor and weak, secretly bound them in rooms, clothed them in cotton garments, shackled and sent to the garrison; the dead were replaced by the escort clerks—every man thought of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Each year Guozhong sent Song Yu, Zheng Ang, and Wei Yan as censors to drive the quotas. County clerks, desperate to meet the numbers, staged sham enlistments, seized the poor and weak, locked them in rooms, dressed them in quilted coats, shackled them, and marched them to the garrisons; when men died the escorts took their place—and everyone seethed with revolt.

sentences.zh: 尋遣劍南留後李宓率兵十餘萬擊閤羅鳳，敗死西洱河，國忠矯為捷書上聞。

translations.literal: Soon he sent Jiannan deputy Li Mi to lead a hundred thousand troops to attack Geluofeng; defeated and died at the western Er River; Guozhong falsified a victory report upward.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he sent Jiannan deputy Li Mi with more than a hundred thousand men against Geluofeng; Mi was defeated and killed at the western Er River, and Guozhong forged a victory report to the throne.

sentences.zh: 自再興師，傾中國驍卒二十萬，踦屨無遺，天下冤之。

translations.literal: From raising the army again, two hundred thousand of the empire's finest soldiers were poured out, not one sandal returned—the realm resented it bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaigns were renewed, two hundred thousand of the empire's best troops were poured out and not a sandal came back—the realm groaned under the injustice.

sentences.zh: 安祿山方有寵，總重兵於邊，偃蹇不奉法，帝護之，下莫敢言。

translations.literal: An Lushan was then in favor, holding heavy armies at the frontier, haughty and not following law; the emperor shielded him; below none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan was then in favor, commanding vast armies on the frontier, arrogant and heedless of law. The emperor shielded him, and below the throne no one dared speak.

sentences.zh: 國忠知終不出己下，又恃內援，獨暴發反狀，帝疑以位相冒，不之信。

translations.literal: Guozhong knew he would in the end not emerge beneath himself, and also relied on inner support; alone he fiercely exposed rebellious signs; the emperor suspected it was ambition contending for rank and did not believe him.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong knew Lushan would never rank beneath him and, relying on his ties within the palace, alone trumpeted evidence of rebellion. The emperor suspected rivalry for position and would not believe him.

sentences.zh: 祿山雖逆久，以帝遇之厚，故隱忍，伺帝一日晏駕則稱兵。

translations.literal: Though Lushan had long been rebellious, because the emperor treated him thickly he therefore concealed himself, waiting until the emperor one day passed away then would raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: Though Lushan had long harbored rebellion, the emperor's lavish favor kept him patient; he waited for the emperor to die, then would raise arms.

sentences.zh: 及見帝嬖國忠，甚畏不利己，故謀日急。

translations.literal: Seeing the emperor favored Guozhong he greatly feared harm to himself; hence the plot grew daily urgent.
translations.idiomatic: When he saw the emperor dote on Guozhong he feared for his own safety, and his plot grew more urgent by the day.

sentences.zh: 俄而祿山授尚書右僕射，帝恐國忠不悅，故冊拜司空。

translations.literal: Shortly Lushan was given the post Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat; fearing Guozhong would not be pleased, therefore he was additionally enfeoffed Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Lushan was made Right Vice Director of the Secretariat; lest Guozhong take offense, the emperor also enfeoffed him Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 祿山還幽州，覺國忠圖己，反謀遂決。

translations.literal: Lushan returned to Youzhou, perceived Guozhong plotted against himself, and the rebellion plot was decided.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan returned to Youzhou, saw that Guozhong was scheming against him, and fixed his mind on rebellion.

sentences.zh: 國忠令客何盈、蹇昂刺求反狀，諷京兆尹李峴圍其第，捕祿山所善李超、安岱、李方來、王岷殺之，貶其黨吉溫於合浦。

translations.literal: Guozhong ordered his guest He Ying and Qian Ang to seek out rebellious evidence, hinting to the Yongzhou magistrate Li Xian to surround his residence, seize and kill those Lushan favored Li Chao, An Dai, Li Fanglai, Wang Min, and demote his partisan Ji Wen to Hepu.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong set his agents He Ying and Qian Ang to hunt for proof of treason and urged Yongzhou magistrate Li Xian to surround Lushan's residence, seize and kill his favorites Li Chao, An Dai, Li Fanglai, and Wang Min, and banish his ally Ji Wen to Hepu.

sentences.zh: 祿山上書自陳，而條上國忠大罪二十，帝歸過於峴，貶零陵太守，以尉祿山意。

translations.literal: Lushan sent up a memorial self-explaining, yet itemized twenty great crimes of Guozhong; the emperor shifted blame to Li Xian, demoted him to Lingling prefect, to appease Lushan's mind.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan memorialized in his own defense but listed twenty capital crimes of Guozhong. The emperor blamed Li Xian instead, demoted him to prefect of Lingling, and tried to soothe Lushan.

sentences.zh: 國忠寡謀矜躁，謂祿山跋扈不足圖，故激怒之使必反，以取信於帝，帝卒不悟。

translations.literal: Guozhong few in strategy, proud and rash, saying Lushan's arrogance was not worth plotting; therefore he provoked him to make him certainly rebel, to gain the emperor's trust—the emperor to the end did not awaken.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong was shallow in counsel and rash with pride, declaring Lushan too arrogant to be worth plotting against; he goaded him into open rebellion to win the emperor's trust—and the emperor never woke to it.

sentences.zh: 乃建言：「請以祿山為平章事，追入輔政，以賈循為使，節度范陽，呂知誨節度平盧，楊光翙節度河東。」

translations.literal: Thereupon he memorialized: "Request appointing Lushan as Co-ordinator of State Affairs, summoning him to enter and assist governance; send Jia Xun as envoy; Xun control Fanyang; Lu Zhiyue control Pinglu; Yang Guanghui control Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He then proposed: "Appoint Lushan Co-ordinator of State Affairs and summon him to court; send Jia Xun as envoy to take over Fanyang, Lu Zhiyue Pinglu, and Yang Guanghui Hedong.

sentences.zh: 已草詔，帝使謁者輔璆琳覘祿山，未還，帝致詔坐側。

translations.literal: The edict was already drafted; the emperor sent Envoy Fu Yulin to observe Lushan; before return the emperor placed the draft edict at his side.
translations.idiomatic: The edict was already drafted. The emperor sent envoy Fu Yulin to observe Lushan; before he returned the draft lay at the emperor's side.

sentences.zh: 而璆琳納金，固言不反。

translations.literal: But Yulin accepted gold and firmly said there would be no rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Yulin took a bribe and swore there would be no rebellion.

sentences.zh: 帝謂國忠曰：「祿山無二心，前詔焚之矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor told Guozhong: "Lushan has no second heart; the previous edict has been burned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Guozhong, "Lushan is loyal. I have burned the earlier edict.

sentences.zh: 祿山反，以誅國忠為名，帝欲自將而東，使皇太子監國，謂左右曰：「我欲行一事。」

translations.literal: Lushan rebelled, taking execution of Guozhong as his banner; the emperor wished to lead the army east himself, making the Crown Prince regent, and told those around: "I wish to do one thing."
translations.idiomatic: Lushan rebelled, naming the execution of Guozhong as his cause. The emperor wished to lead the eastern campaign himself and make the crown prince regent. He told his attendants, "I mean to do one thing."

sentences.zh: 國忠揣帝且禪太子，歸謂女弟等曰：「太子監國，吾屬誅矣。」

translations.literal: Guozhong guessed the emperor would abdicate to the crown prince; returning he told his sisters: "The crown prince as regent—we are marked for execution."
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong guessed the emperor meant to abdicate to the crown prince. He went home and told his sisters, "If the crown prince becomes regent, we are dead."

sentences.zh: 因聚泣，入訴於貴妃，妃以死邀帝，遂寢。

translations.literal: Thereupon they gathered weeping; entering they appealed to the Noble Consort; the consort with her life pressed the emperor—the plan was laid to rest.
translations.idiomatic: They gathered and wept, then went to Yang Guifei and pleaded with her. She threatened her own life before the emperor, and the plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 祿山既發范陽，嘆咤曰：「國忠頭來何遲？」

translations.literal: Lushan having launched from Fanyang sighed: "Why is Guozhong's head so slow in coming?"
translations.idiomatic: Once Lushan marched from Fanyang he sighed, "Why is Guozhong's head so slow to arrive?"

sentences.zh: 哥舒翰守潼關，按兵守險，國忠聞欲反己，疑之，乃從中督戰，翰不得已出關，遂大敗，降賊。

translations.literal: Geshu Han guarded Tong Pass, holding troops and guarding the peril; Guozhong heard he wished to rebel against himself and suspected him; then from within he supervised the battle—Han had no choice but to leave the pass and was greatly defeated, surrendering to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Geshu Han held Tong Pass, keeping his army on the defensible ground. Guozhong heard he meant to turn against him and grew suspicious, then pressed the battle from court. Han had no choice but to leave the pass, was routed, and surrendered to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 書聞，是日帝自南內移仗未央宮。

translations.literal: When the report arrived, that day the emperor moved his presence from the southern inner palace to Weiyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When word came, that same day the emperor moved from the southern inner palace to Weiyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 國忠見百官，鯁咽不自勝。

translations.literal: Guozhong saw the hundred officials, choking and unable to bear himself.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong faced the officials, sobbing he could scarcely hold himself together.

sentences.zh: 監察御史高適請率百官子弟及募豪桀十萬拒守，眾以為不可。

translations.literal: Supervising Censor Gao Shi requested to lead sons of hundred officials and recruited brave fellows a hundred thousand to resist and hold; the multitude deemed it impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising censor Gao Shi asked to lead the sons of officials and ten thousand recruited braves to hold the capital; the crowd judged it impossible.

sentences.zh: 初，國忠聞難作，自以身帥劍南，豫置腹心梁、益間，為自完計。

translations.literal: At first when Guozhong heard trouble had arisen he thought to lead troops himself to Jiannan, pre-positioning trusted men between Liang and Yi, as a plan to preserve himself.
translations.idiomatic: When trouble first broke out Guozhong had planned to lead troops to Jiannan himself, planting trusted men between Liang and Yi as a refuge.

sentences.zh: 至是，帝召宰相計事，國忠曰：「幸蜀便。」

translations.literal: Reaching this the emperor summoned chancellors to plan affairs; Guozhong said: "Going to Shu would be convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Now the emperor summoned the chancellors to deliberate; Guozhong said, "Flight to Shu would be best.

sentences.zh: 帝然之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 明日遲昕，帝出延秋門，群臣不知，猶上朝，唯三衛廣騎立仗，尚聞刻漏聲。

translations.literal: Next day dawn was late; the emperor went out Yongqiu Gate; the hundred officials did not know, still attending court; only the three guards and broad cavalry stood formation; still heard the clepsydra's drip.
translations.idiomatic: The next morning dawn came late. The emperor went out Yongqiu Gate; the officials knew nothing and still attended court—only the three guards and the broad cavalry stood watch, and the water-clock still dripped.

sentences.zh: 國忠與韋見素、高力士及皇太子諸王數百人護帝。

translations.literal: Guozhong with Wei Jiansu, Gao Lishi, the crown prince, various princes—several hundred people guarded the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong went with Wei Jiansu, Gao Lishi, the crown prince, the princes, and several hundred others to guard the emperor.

sentences.zh: 右龍武大將軍陳玄禮謀殺國忠，不克。

translations.literal: Right Dragon Martial Grand General Chen Xuanli plotted to kill Guozhong but did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Right Dragon Martial Grand General Chen Xuanli plotted to kill Guozhong but failed.

sentences.zh: 進次馬嵬，將士疲，乏食，玄禮懼亂，召諸將曰：「今天子震蕩，社稷不守，使生人肝腦塗地，豈非國忠所致！

translations.literal: Advancing to Mawei; the officers and soldiers weary, food lacking; Xuanli feared chaos and called the generals: "Today the Son of Heaven is shaken, the altars not preserved, making living men's livers and guts smear the ground—is it not from Guozhong!
translations.idiomatic: At Mawei the troops were exhausted and starving. Xuanli feared mutiny and called the generals: "The Son of Heaven is shaken, the altars in peril, and men's lives are ground into the dust—is this not Guozhong's doing?

sentences.zh: 欲誅之以謝天下，雲何？」

translations.literal: Wishing to execute him to apologize to the realm, what say you?
translations.idiomatic: I would kill him to answer to the realm. What say you?

sentences.zh: 眾曰：「念之久矣，事行身死，固所願。」

translations.literal: The multitude said: "We have long wished it; to act though the body dies is our fixed wish."
translations.idiomatic: They cried, "We have wanted this for ages; even if we die in the act, we are content."

sentences.zh: 會吐蕃使有請於國忠，眾大呼曰：「國忠與吐蕃謀反！」

translations.literal: It happened a Tibetan envoy had business with Guozhong; the multitude shouted: "Guozhong and the Tibetans plot rebellion!"
translations.idiomatic: Just then a Tibetan envoy came to see Guozhong. The crowd roared, "Guozhong is plotting with the Tibetans!"

sentences.zh: 衛騎合，國忠突出，或射中其頞，殺之，爭啖其肉且盡，梟首以徇。

translations.literal: The guard cavalry combined; Guozhong rushed out; some shot and struck his brow; they killed him, contending to eat his flesh nearly to exhaustion, displayed the head to show.
translations.idiomatic: The guards closed in. Guozhong bolted out; someone shot him in the brow and they killed him, tearing at his flesh until little remained, then paraded his head.

sentences.zh: 帝驚曰：「國忠遂反耶？」

translations.literal: The emperor startled: "Guozhong has rebelled then?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor cried in shock, "So Guozhong has rebelled?

sentences.zh: 時吐蕃使亦殲矣。

translations.literal: At the time the Tibetan envoy was also destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetan envoy was killed as well.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫魏方進責眾曰：「何故殺宰相？」

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Wei Fangjin rebuked the multitude: "Why kill the chancellor?
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Wei Fangjin rebuked the mob: "Why kill the chancellor?

sentences.zh: 眾怒，又殺之。

translations.literal: The multitude angry, killed him too.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, they killed him too.

sentences.zh: 四子：暄、出、曉、晞。

translations.literal: Four sons: Xuan, Chu, Xiao, Xi.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: Xuan, Chu, Xiao, and Xi.

sentences.zh: 暄位太常卿、戶部侍郎，聞亂，下馬蹶，弩眾射之，身貫百矢，乃踣。

translations.literal: Xuan held Grand Master of Splendor and Vice Minister of Revenue; hearing of the turmoil he dismounted his horse and stumbled; the rebellious troops shot him; a hundred arrows pierced his body before he fell.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was Grand Master of Splendor and Vice Minister of Revenue. When he heard of the upheaval he fell from his horse; rebel archers shot him until a hundred arrows had pierced him and he collapsed.

sentences.zh: 出尚萬春公主，位鴻臚卿，陷賊見殺。

translations.literal: Chu married the Princess of Wanchun, held Director of the Court for Diplomatic Relations; caught in rebellion was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Chu had married the Princess of Wanchun and was Director of the Court for Diplomatic Relations; he was caught in the rebellion and killed.

sentences.zh: 曉奔漢中，為漢中王瑀搒死。

translations.literal: Xiao fled to Hanzhong, was clubbed to death by Prince of Hanzhong Wang Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao fled to Hanzhong and was beaten to death by the Prince of Hanzhong, Wang Yu.

sentences.zh: 晞及國忠妻裴柔同奔陳倉，為追兵所斬。

translations.literal: Xi and Guozhong's wife Pei Rou together fled to Chencang, were beheaded by pursuing troops.
translations.idiomatic: Xi and Guozhong's wife Pei Rou fled together to Chencang and were beheaded by pursuers.

sentences.zh: 柔，故蜀倡也，並坎而瘞。

translations.literal: Rou was formerly a Shu singer; all were buried together in one pit.
translations.idiomatic: Rou had once been a singing girl in Shu; they were buried together in one pit.

sentences.zh: 其黨翰林學士張漸、竇華，中書舍人宋昱，吏部郎中鄭昂，俱走山谷，民爭其貲，富埒國忠。

translations.literal: His partisans Hanlin Academician Zhang Jian, Dou Hua, Secretariat Drafter Song Yu, Ministry of Personnel Director Zheng Ang—altogether fled to valleys; the people scrambled for their goods, wealth rivaling Guozhong.
translations.idiomatic: His followers—Hanlin academician Zhang Jian, Dou Hua, Secretariat drafter Song Yu, Ministry director Zheng Ang—all fled into the hills. The people looted their goods, fortunes rivaling Guozhong's own.

sentences.zh: 昱戀貲產，竊入都，為亂兵所殺；

translations.literal: Yu clung to goods and property, secretly entered the capital, was killed by rebellious troops;
translations.idiomatic: Song Yu, unable to abandon his wealth, stole back into the capital and was killed by rebel soldiers;

sentences.zh: 餘坐誅。

translations.literal: the rest sat punishment and were executed.
translations.idiomatic: the rest were tried and executed.

sentences.zh: 國忠本名釗，以圖讖有「卯金刀」，當位御史中丞時，帝為改今名。

translations.literal: Guozhong's original name was Zhao; because prognostic texts had "mao-metal-knife," when he reached Censor-in-Chief the emperor changed his present name for him.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong's birth name was Zhao; because prophecy spoke of "mao-metal-knife," when he became Censor-in-Chief the emperor gave him his present name.

sentences.zh: 李翛，字翛，起寒賤，由莊憲太后婭婿得進，歷坊、絳二州刺史。

translations.literal: Li Xiao, style Xiao, rose from cold poverty; through being the Zhuangxian Empress's niece's husband he gained advancement, serving as prefect of Fang and Jiang two prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiao, whose style was also Xiao, rose from humble poverty. As son-in-law to a niece of Empress Zhuangxian he advanced, and served as prefect of Fang and Jiang.

sentences.zh: 無它才，為政粗辦。

translations.literal: No other talent; in governing affairs he handled things roughly adequately.
translations.idiomatic: He had no other gift; in office he managed affairs in a rough but passable way.

sentences.zh: 性纖巧，飾廚傳，結納閹寺，求善譽。

translations.literal: Nature delicate and clever, adorning kitchen relays, forming ties with palace eunuchs, seeking good reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Delicate and clever by nature, he stocked fine kitchens and curried favor with palace eunuchs to win a good name.

sentences.zh: 憲宗以為才，拜伺農卿，進京兆尹，專聚斂以固恩寵，數譖毀近臣，一時側目。

translations.literal: Xianzong thought him talented, appointed Director of Agriculture, advanced to Yongzhou magistrate, exclusively amassing levies to secure favor and grace, repeatedly slandering close officials—at one time all eyes turned sidelong.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong judged him capable, made him Director of Agriculture, then Yongzhou magistrate. He piled up levies to secure imperial favor and slandered courtiers at will—until everyone watched him with narrowed eyes.

sentences.zh: 太后崩，詔翛為橋道置頓使，嗇官費，物物裁損為可喜者。

translations.literal: When the empress dowager died, an edict made Xiao commissioner for establishing halts on the bridge route; he was stingy with official funds and trimmed every item to what might please.
translations.idiomatic: After the empress dowager's death Li Xiao was made commissioner for funeral halts along the bridge route; he skimped on official funds and pared every expense down to what might look impressive.

sentences.zh: 梓宮至灞橋，從官多不得食。

translations.literal: When the imperial coffin reached Ba Bridge, many of the attending officials could not obtain food.
translations.idiomatic: When the coffin reached Ba Bridge, many in the funeral train went without food.

sentences.zh: 始議更造渭城門，計錢三萬，翛以為勞，不聽，使鑿軌道深之，柱危不支，方過喪而門壞，辒京僅免，徹門乃得行。

translations.literal: At first they discussed rebuilding the Weicheng gate, estimating thirty thousand cash; Xiao thought it laborious and would not agree, and had the track channel dug deeper; the pillars were perilously unsupported; just as the funeral passed the gate collapsed; the imperial hearse barely escaped; only after removing the gate could they proceed.
translations.idiomatic: They first planned to rebuild the Weicheng gate at a cost of thirty thousand cash; Xiao called it too much work and refused, ordering the cart track cut deeper instead; the gateposts gave way; as the funeral train passed the gate collapsed and the imperial hearse barely escaped—only after tearing the gate down could the procession move on.

sentences.zh: 翛妄奏車軸折，山陵使李逢吉劾罔上，請免官。

translations.literal: Xiao falsely memorialized that an axle had broken; the mausoleum commissioner Li Fengji impeached him for deceiving the sovereign and requested dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao falsely reported a broken axle; Li Fengji, commissioner for the imperial tomb, impeached him for deceiving the throne and asked that he be removed.

sentences.zh: 方帝用兵而翛屢有所獻，得不坐，才詔奪稟，逢吉持之，乃削銀青一階。

translations.literal: Just then the emperor was using troops and Xiao had repeatedly made offerings, so he escaped punishment; only an edict stripped his salary allotment; Fengji pressed the case, and one grade of silver and cyan was cut.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was at war and Xiao had made repeated gifts, so he escaped dismissal; an edict merely cut his stipend, but Fengji pressed on and one grade of his silver-cyan rank was taken.

sentences.zh: 翌日，加賜黃金。

translations.literal: The next day additional gold was bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor added a gift of gold.

sentences.zh: 帝以浙西富饒，欲掊捃遺利，以翛為觀察使。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Zhexi was rich and fertile, wished to squeeze out leftover profit and made Xiao its observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zhexi was wealthy the emperor wanted to squeeze out every surplus profit and made Xiao its observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 被疾還京師。

translations.literal: He fell ill and returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill and returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 元和十四年卒，士有相賀者。

translations.literal: He died in the fourteenth year of Yuanhe; among the gentlemen some congratulated one another.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 819, and some scholars openly rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 鄭光，孝明皇太后弟也。

translations.literal: Zheng Guang was the younger brother of Empress Dowager Xiaoming.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Guang was the younger brother of Empress Dowager Xiaoming.

sentences.zh: 會昌末，夢禦大車載日月行中衢，光輝洪洞照六合，寤而占之，工曰：「君且暴貴。」

translations.literal: At the end of the Huichang era he dreamed of driving a great carriage bearing the sun and moon through the middle of the crossroads, their radiance vast and flooding, illuminating the six directions; on waking he had it divined, and the artisan said: "My lord is about to rise suddenly to high rank.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Huichang he dreamed he drove a great cart bearing the sun and moon through the city's central crossing, their light flooding the world; when he woke and had it interpreted, the diviner said, "You are about to rise suddenly to great honor.

sentences.zh: 不闋月，宣宗即位，光興民伍，拜諸衛將軍，遷累平盧軍節度使，徙河中、鳳翔，又賜鄠、雲陽二縣良田。

translations.literal: Within less than a month Xuanzong took the throne; Guang rose from the common ranks, was appointed a general of the guards, was repeatedly transferred to military governor of the Pinglu army, moved to Hezhong and Fengxiang, and was further granted fertile fields in Hu and Yunyang counties.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month Xuanzong had taken the throne; Guang rose from common life, became a guards general, served as military governor of Pinglu, then Hezhong and Fengxiang, and was granted rich lands in Hu and Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 大中四年，詔除其租賦，宰相言：「國常賦，窶人下戶不免，柰何以外戚廢法？」

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dazhong an edict remitted his rents and levies; the chancellor said: "The state's regular levies—even poor households on the lower registers are not exempt—how can we void the law for maternal kin?
translations.idiomatic: In 850 an edict exempted his rents and taxes; the chancellor objected: "The state's regular taxes are not waived even for the poorest households—how can we suspend the law for an imperial in-law?

sentences.zh: 帝悟，追格前詔。

translations.literal: The emperor understood and revoked the earlier edict.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took the point and withdrew the earlier edict.

sentences.zh: 俄封其妾為夫人，光曉帝意，還詔不敢拜，帝嘉之。

translations.literal: Soon his concubine was enfeoffed as a lady; Guang understood the emperor's intent, returned the edict and dared not accept the title, and the emperor praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his concubine was made a lady; Guang sensed the emperor's intent, returned the patent and declined the title, and the emperor commended him.

sentences.zh: 七年，來朝，對延英，占奏俚近，帝失所望，不悅，留為右羽林統軍兼太子太保。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he came to court, answered at Yanying Hall, and his prognostications and memorials were vulgar and shallow; the emperor lost hope and was displeased, and kept him as commander of the Right Forest Guard with concurrent Grand Protector of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he came to court and spoke at Yanying Hall in crude, shallow terms; the emperor was disappointed and displeased and kept him in the capital as commander of the Right Forest Guard and Grand Protector of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 太后言其家空短，帝厚賜金繒，終不復委方鎮。

translations.literal: The empress dowager said his household was poor and short of means; the emperor richly bestowed gold and silks, but never again entrusted him with a frontier command.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager said his family was poor; the emperor gave him lavish gifts of gold and silk but never again sent him to a regional command.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈司徒，詔罷三日朝，群臣奉慰。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made Minister of Education; an edict suspended court for three days and the ministers offered condolences.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Minister of Education; court was suspended for three days while the ministers offered condolences.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫李景讓曰：「禮，外祖父母、舅服小功五月，伯叔父若兄弟齊缞期，所以疏外密內也。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Li Jingrang said: "By ritual, for maternal grandparents and uncles one wears xiaogong mourning for five months; for father's brothers or brothers one wears qizhui for the full term—thus what is outside is kept distant and what is inside is kept close.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Li Jingrang said, "By ritual, maternal grandparents and uncles receive five months of lesser mourning, while paternal uncles and brothers receive the full mourning period—keeping the outer circle distant and the inner circle close.

sentences.zh: 王者不可使外戚強。

translations.literal: A king must not allow maternal kin to grow strong.
translations.idiomatic: A sovereign must not let his in-laws grow powerful.

sentences.zh: 按王、公主喪不過三日，光宜少降。」

translations.literal: According to precedent, mourning for kings and princesses does not exceed three days; Guang's should be somewhat reduced.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent princes and princesses receive no more than three days of mourning; Guang's observance should be reduced accordingly.

sentences.zh: 詔罷二日。

translations.literal: An edict suspended court for two days.
translations.idiomatic: An edict cut the suspension to two days.

sentences.zh: 子漢卿，終義昌軍節度使。

translations.literal: His son Hanqing ended as military governor of the Yichang army.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hanqing ended his career as military governor of Yichang.
